heading: Error Catalog
text: # Error Catalog

heading: The 3 standing FE rules
text:
## The 3 standing FE rules

1. **HTTP status as primary routing signal** (400/401/409/422/423/429)
2. **Display localized `errorMessages[0]`** from `ServiceOperationResult<T>`
3. **Never parse error codes** for branching UI copy — codes are for logging only

heading: Status → UX response mapping
text:
## Status → UX response mapping

| Status | What it means | Typical UX |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | Missing/malformed field | Inline field error |
| 401 | Unauthorized | Redirect to login |
| 403 | Forbidden (rare; mostly PES) | Toast |
| 409 | Conflict (duplicate) | Inline field error |
| 422 | Business rule violation | Inline message or toast |
| 423 | User locked | Full-screen lockout page |
| 429 | Rate limit (OTP cooldown / resend) | Disable resend + countdown |

heading: Defensive coding patterns (canonical)
text:
## Defensive coding patterns (canonical)

- **Charging cascade differentiation**: `InsufficientBalance` vs `NoApplicableRate` vs `ReservationNotFound` vs `WalletVersionConflict` — different UX per code
- **Lockout cascade**: IP gate → eligibility → credentials → OTP (each error has its own surface)
- **Idempotency-as-success**: `AlreadyApplied = true` on Charging 200 responses must NOT be treated as error
- **Add Client Step 5 partial-failure**: Account is created **before** Identity hop fires; surface "Account created but Account Owner creation failed — contact support"

heading: The 4 flows
text:
## The 4 flows

| Flow | Trigger | Allowed roles | Steps | PRD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Add Client** | Org-hierarchy "Add Client" button | sys-admin · sys-products | 5 wizard steps | PRD-01 |
| **Add User** | Org-hierarchy "Add User" button | sys-admin · sys-products · sys-ops · acc-owner · acc-admin (scope-varying) | 3 wizard tabs | PRD-02 |
| **Add Node** | Org-hierarchy "Add Sub-Node" button | sys-admin · sys-products · sys-ops · acc-owner · acc-admin | inline | PRD-01 |
| **Edit Node** | Org-hierarchy "Edit Node" action | same as Add Node | inline + scheduled rename | PRD-01 |

heading: Three-actor-path clarification (Add User)
text:
## Three-actor-path clarification (Add User)

The Add User wizard's Tab 2 Role dropdown is populated from `POST /pes/authorize/resources` (not a static client-side enum). The dropdown contents depend on the actor:

| Actor | Can grant which roles? |
|---|---|
| sys-admin · sys-products | Any role (any sys-* or any acc-*) |
| sys-ops | Own role + all acc-* |
| acc-owner | All acc-* (one acc-owner per tenant rule — BR-UM-03) |
| acc-admin | Only acc-admin + acc-user (cannot promote to acc-owner) |
| acc-user | Cannot add users at all |

heading: Critical drift surfaced across all 4 flows
text:
## Critical drift surfaced across all 4 flows

- **Username 30 vs 100 cap** — PRD BR-UM-12 says 30, backend FluentValidation says 100 → FE must enforce 30
- **PasswordSecurityLevel vocabulary** — PRD `Normal/Advanced` vs backend `Low/Medium/High/Strict` (Q-UM-12)

heading: Add Client Step 5 partial-failure trap
text:
## Add Client Step 5 partial-failure trap

Account is persisted server-side **before** the Identity hop fires. If Identity creation fails, you have an orphan Account record. FE must surface: "Account created but Account Owner creation failed — contact support" and preserve wizard state for retry.

heading: Implementation Pitfalls
text: # Implementation Pitfalls

heading: The 5 pitfall categories
text:
## The 5 pitfall categories

| Category | Count | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Permission** | 7 | deny-by-omission · scope-arg factory · `app.*.view` hidden gate · expression-gated rules · Wave 1.3.0 ghost keys · default-deny `allowedActions` · "PES passes but feature key denies" |
| **B. Validation** | 6 | FE-tighter-than-backend drift · missing `[ThrowIf*]` · 3-layer collapse · async debounce · error-code-switching · OTP TTL relative-vs-absolute |
| **C. Data** | 5 | Mongo ID vs Zitadel ID universe · DTO enrichment asymmetry · type-flip drift · status enum int divergence · mixed casing |
| **D. View-hide** | 4 | composite gate semantics · tab-visibility reversal · default-deny `allowedActions` · 6 gate types collapsed |
| **E. Cross-service** | 3 | currency enum drift · duplicated validation · TS-vs-C# enum divergence |

heading: The 13 anti-patterns (from old UI)
text:
## The 13 anti-patterns (from old UI)

| # | Anti-pattern | Replace with |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SCSS files everywhere | Tailwind utilities only |
| 2 | PrimeNG components | Falcon UI Core (`<falcon-*>`) |
| 3 | PrimeIcons (`pi pi-*`) | `<falcon-icon>` / `<falcon-svg-icon>` |
| 4 | `@Input` / `@Output` decorators | `input()` / `output()` signal APIs |
| 5 | `*ngIf` / `*ngFor` | `@if` / `@for` |
| 6 | Hand-rolled HTML strings in render fns | Angular templates / `ng-template` |
| 7 | `alert()` calls | `MessageService` or Falcon dialog |
| 8 | PascalCase request bodies | Backend-normalized or uniform serializer |
| 9 | Silent `return of([])` after delay | Log + propagate via `ServiceOperationResult` |
| 10 | Magic-string defaults (IP list, icons, `'EMPTY'`) | Constants |
| 11 | Cross-feature sibling imports (`../../../../../`) | Promote to `libs/falcon` |
| 12 | `as any` casts for response shapes | Fully type response DTOs |
| 13 | Mixed template-driven + reactive forms | Reactive throughout |

heading: The cheat sheet — "if I see X, check Y first"
text:
## The cheat sheet — "if I see X, check Y first"

| Symptom | First place to look |
|---|---|
| User logs in but sees no pages | `app.*.view` PES key (the hidden gate) |
| PES check returns deny silently for every page | PES `g`-rule subject — must be `u:<JWT.sub>@<ns>`, NEVER Mongo `_id` |
| acc-admin can see services UI (should not) | `acc.services.view` returns explicit deny — but UI didn't gate on it |
| Form submits but backend returns 422 | Missing cross-field validator (FormGroup level) |
| Field validates client-side but rejects server-side | Drift between FE rule and backend `[ThrowIf*]` attribute |
| Username accepted at 50 chars (should be 30) | FE not enforcing tighter cap — PRD says 30, backend says 100 |
| Wallet transfer fails with currency error | `V-charging-transfer-source-destination` — wallets must match currency |
| Status enum int doesn't match across services | Commerce vs Provisioning use different ints for same names |
| Contact-group share dropped silently | `SharedWithAllUsers=true` + `SharedUsers[]` mutex (BR-CGM-09/10) |
| Payment poll runs forever | Hard 30-min upper bound; check `SimplePoll.watch` config |

purpose: "Answers 'what 4 protocols + 1 script must run for unsupervised AI work to be safe'. Open before starting any night-shift task; consulted at every fork during the build."
---

> [!tldr]
> 4 protocols + 1 chained-verification script that turn the authority dataset from ~80% night-shift-ready to ~95%. Without these, autonomous AI shifts produce ambiguous specs, arbitrary fork resolutions, visually-wrong UI, and false-positive "done" claims.

heading: Night-Shift Readiness
text: # Night-Shift Readiness

heading: The 4 protocols
text:
## The 4 protocols

| Protocol | Answers | When invoked |
|---|---|---|
| **SPEC-PROTOCOL** | "How do I turn prose into a falsifiable SPEC.md?" | Step 1 — before any code |
| **DECISION-PROTOCOL** | "When the AI hits a fork, which rule applies + when to halt?" | Step 2 — during plan + during build |
| **VISUAL-TARGETS** | "What should feature F LOOK like — components, tokens, states?" | Step 3 — before writing UI code |
| **NIGHT-SHIFT-LOOP** | "How does the AI chain build → scanner → backend verify → done-or-halt?" | Step 4 — automated verification |

heading: The 5-check readiness gate
text:
## The 5-check readiness gate

Before running ANY task in night-shift mode, all 5 must be 🟢:

1. **SPEC ready** — task has a complete `SPEC.md` per SPEC-PROTOCOL (or task is a port/playbook with locked scope)
2. **Decision protocol applies** — every fork the task will hit has a rule OR is in the conservative-defaults catalog
3. **Visual target exists** — task has a visual fidelity reference (old-UI · wireframe · component default)
4. **Verification automatable** — task can be checked via `nx build` + scanner + backend PES verify
5. **Decision-log destination ready** — `_runtime-verification/decisions-<date>.md` will be auto-populated

If any of these 5 is 🔴, the task is **not safe for night-shift** — escalate to a supervised session.

heading: The 25-fork catalog (DECISION-PROTOCOL highlights)
text:
## The 25-fork catalog (DECISION-PROTOCOL highlights)

| Class | Count | Default escalation |
|---|---|---|
| A — Authority | 5 | Halt-and-flag |
| B — Validation | 6 | Apply rule or default |
| C — Entity drift | 3 | Apply rule (PRD wins on labels) |
| D — Business rule | 5 | Apply rule or halt |
| E — UI/UX | 4 | Apply conservative default |
| F — Operational | 3 | Halt-and-flag |

Each fork has: name · class · trigger · canonical resolution · escalation criteria · logging.

heading: The 12 conservative defaults (SPEC-PROTOCOL highlights)
text:
## The 12 conservative defaults (SPEC-PROTOCOL highlights)

For common forks where the rule is clear but the spec doesn't say it explicitly: username cap (PRD wins · 30) · PasswordSecurityLevel mapping · empty-state shown not hidden · loading state = skeleton not spinner · error UI inline + toast · locale fallback en-US · date format ISO 8601 transport / PRD display · boolean default false · enum first non-None · pagination size 20 · status badge color per `02-statuses/<entity>-status.md`.

heading: Visual fidelity hierarchy (VISUAL-TARGETS rule)
text:
## Visual fidelity hierarchy (VISUAL-TARGETS rule)

If sources disagree on what the UI should look like:
1. **Old-UI proven implementation** wins (shipped + worked)
2. **PRD wireframe** (if available)
3. **Falcon UI Core component default** (unstyled baseline)
4. **AI inference** (last resort — must flag as Class E fork)

heading: The 4-gate loop (NIGHT-SHIFT-LOOP)
text:
## The 4-gate loop (NIGHT-SHIFT-LOOP)

```
Gate 1 — nx build green
Gate 2 — scan-authority -CheckOnly clean
Gate 3 — Backend PES verify (login + authorize for users defined in SPEC)
Gate 4 — Done marker (completion report + decisions log)
[Gate 5 — FE runtime: DEFERRED on workspace compile errors]
```

Each gate has an explicit exit code (0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 10 / 99). Halts produce a `_pending-questions/<task>.md` instead of fake completion.

purpose: "Answers 'which 6 non-PES gate types (session-type, node-type, mode, tab-visibility, server-driven, composite) apply to each feature'. Open before porting any UI."
---

> [!tldr]
> The 6 non-PES gate types catalogued per feature. PES is one of many gates — UI hiding usually composes 2-4 gate types together. Composite gates like `canEditSelectedSettings` are the canonical pattern.

heading: Non-PES Gates × Feature
text: # Non-PES Gates × Feature

heading: The 6 gate types
text:
## The 6 gate types

| Gate | Mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **PES** | Policy decision | `FalconAccess.adminConsole.account.add()` |
| **Session-type** | JWT user-type claim | `session.userType === FALCON_USER` |
| **Node-type** | Tree position flag | `isFalconNode`, `isFirstLevelChild`, `isRootSelection`, `isMainMenu` |
| **Mode** | Component state | `mode === HierarchyTabMode.View` |
| **Tab-visibility** | Computed in tabs-layout | `enabled: !isFalcon && isMain` |
| **Server-driven row** | Backend stamps per-row | `row.allowedActions: FalconRowAction[]` |
| **Composite** | All of the above AND'd | `canEditSelectedSettings` = PES + isMainNodeSelection + isRootSelection + business rule |

heading: Composite gate canonical example
text:
## Composite gate canonical example

```typescript
get canEditSelectedSettings(): boolean {
  return this.canEditPasswordSecurityLevel    // PES flag
      && (this.isRootSelection                  // node-type
          || this.isMainNodeSelection)          // node-type
      && this.mode === HierarchyTabMode.Edit;   // mode
}
```

This is why pure PES checks are insufficient — node-type business rules compose on top.

heading: Server-driven row pattern
text:
## Server-driven row pattern

Marketplace + Comms-hub stamp `row.allowedActions: FalconRowAction[]` server-side per row. FE trusts the backend — no client-side `canDo*` flags for row-level decisions. Pattern preserved across admin → mgmt port.

heading: Why this matters for porting (admin → mgmt)
text:
## Why this matters for porting (admin → mgmt)

| Gate type | Difference on mgmt side |
|---|---|
| Session-type | Fixed CLIENT_USER (not FALCON_USER) — invert conditions |
| Node-type | Mgmt has no synthetic Falcon root — drop `isFalconNode` checks |
| Tab-visibility | `!isFalcon && isMain` becomes always-true → simplify or drop |
| Composite gates | Often simpler on mgmt (fewer business-rule layers) |

> [!tldr]
> Three artefacts close the gap between "brain exists" and "brain is used". An onboarding protocol takes new contributors from zero → productive in ~3 hours. A PR template forces every change to declare its brain-grounding. A readiness checklist (12 yes/no gates) walks through pre-flight per session.

heading: Onboarding
text: # Onboarding

heading: How the three relate
text:
## How the three relate

```
First session ever  →  ONBOARDING-PROTOCOL (one-time, day 1)
                            ↓
Every session       →  READINESS-CHECKLIST (12 gates, ~3min)
                            ↓
Every PR            →  PR-TEMPLATE (forced brain-grounding)
```

heading: ONBOARDING-PROTOCOL — 5 steps
text:
## ONBOARDING-PROTOCOL — 5 steps

| Step | Duration | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Topology | 30min | Know what exists + agent roster |
| 2. Authority | 45min | Understand Falcon-vs-Client + 1 feature deeply |
| 3. Protocols | 30min | Know what to do at any fork |
| 4. Tools | 30min | Run the daily-driver scripts |
| 5. First change | 60-90min | Ship a brain-grounded change end-to-end |

Drill into [ONBOARDING-PROTOCOL](../_mounts/brain-outputs/datasets/authority-dataset/21-onboarding/ONBOARDING-PROTOCOL.md) for the file-list per step.

heading: READINESS-CHECKLIST — 12 gates per session
text:
## READINESS-CHECKLIST — 12 gates per session

Before writing code, all 12 must be Y:

| # | Gate | Y means |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Read MASTER-INDEX this session | Can route a question to the right cluster |
| 2 | Read VERIFICATION-STATUS this session | Know runtime-verified vs structurally-checked |
| 3 | Not claiming runtime status for a structural-only fact | No "shipped"/"validated" without runtime evidence |
| 4 | Know which kingdom (admin/mgmt) is affected | sys-* vs acc-* role |
| 5 | Know which PES keys are touched | Listed by name, not "permissions" |
| 6 | Know which V-rules cross | Listed by id (V-AC-01 etc.) or N/A justified |
| 7 | Know which BR-* bind | Listed by id or N/A justified |
| 8 | Know entity drift items | PRD label vs backend prop vs FE label |
| 9 | Consulted right flow playbook | Brain SK folder/file listed |
| 10 | Identified relevant pitfalls | At least 1 pitfall named, or none-apply justified |
| 11 | Have a visual target (if UI) | Old-UI / wireframe / component / flagged-INFERRED |
| 12 | Will source-prefix every Falcon fact | The convention |

Drill into [READINESS-CHECKLIST](../_mounts/brain-outputs/datasets/authority-dataset/21-onboarding/READINESS-CHECKLIST.md) for what to do when a gate fails.

heading: PR-TEMPLATE — required brain-grounding declaration
text:
## PR-TEMPLATE — required brain-grounding declaration

Every PR description must contain 5 sections:

1. **What this PR changes** — 1-sentence outcome
2. **Brain artefacts consulted** — checkboxes for every cluster the change touches
3. **Source-prefix audit** — 3 random facts with their `[CODE]`/`[BRAIN-OUT]`/etc. tag
4. **Decisions at forks** — table: fork × class × resolution × source
5. **Did NOT verify** — explicit list of unknowns the reviewer can scrutinise
6. **Memory-grow** — what was added (or why not)
7. **Verification** — audit clean + scanner clean + build green

PRs without this template are rejected by reviewers — even one-line typos need Sections 1, 2, and the source-prefix audit.

Drill into [PR-TEMPLATE](../_mounts/brain-outputs/datasets/authority-dataset/21-onboarding/PR-TEMPLATE.md) for the full copy-paste template.

heading: Audience map
text:
## Audience map

| You are | Use which artefact |
|---|---|
| New human contributor | All 3 (ONBOARDING → READINESS → PR) |
| Fresh AI session on Falcon | ONBOARDING (read once after SessionStart) then READINESS each session |
| Returning after >30 days | ONBOARDING as a refresher |
| Cross-team rotation | Skip ONBOARDING Step 1; Step 2 + 3 for new domain |
| Reviewer | PR-TEMPLATE — enforce it |

heading: Policy subject build (FE)
Two ID universes — do not confuse
text:
## Two ID universes — do not confuse

| ID | Where it lives | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `JWT.sub` | JWT claim | PES policy subject (**only this matters for authorization**) |
| `Mongo _id` | Identity Users doc | Identity internals (cross-refs, profile lookups) |
| `identityUserId` field | Identity Users doc | = Zitadel id (synthesises the link) |

> 🔴 Standing rule: PES `g`-rule subject MUST be `u:<ZitadelUserId>@<ns>` — NEVER `u:<MongoId>@<ns>`. Wrong subject = silent deny everywhere. See [[PES-Subject-Contract]].

heading: Status enums
text: # Status enums

heading: Statuses by entity
text:
## Statuses by entity

| Entity | Enum | Values | Service |
|---|---|---|---|
| User | `eUserStatus` | Pending(1) / Active(2) / Suspended(3) / Locked(4) / Deleted(5) | Identity + Commerce (duplicated) |
| Account creation | `eAccountCreationStatus` | Pending(1) → InfoCompleted(2) → SettingsCompleted(3) → ServicesConfigured(4) → AppsConfigured(5) → OwnerCreated(6) → Completed(7) | Commerce |
| Service (Commerce) | `eFalconServiceStatus` | None(0) / InActive(1) / Active(2) / Expired(3) / Disabled(4) | Commerce |
| Service subscription | `eProductSubscriptionStatus` | InActive(1) / Paid(2) / Active(3) / Expired(4) / Disabled(5) | Provisioning ⚠️ different ints than Commerce |
| Contract | `eContractStatus` | Pending(1) / Active(2) / Expired(3) | Commerce |
| Order | `eOrderStatus` | Pending(1) / Paid(2) / Failed(3) | Commerce |
| Job | `eJobStatus` | Scheduled(1) / Executed(2) / Failed(3) / Canceled(4) | Commerce (auto-renewal) |
| Auth stage | `eAuthenticationStage` | PasswordPending(1) → OtpPending(2) → PasswordChangeRequired(3) → Authenticated(4) → Failed(5) → PasswordResetPending(6) | Identity |
| Node type | `eNodeType` | Main(1) / Sub(2) | Commerce (structural, not status) |

heading: Key supporting enums (classification, not status)
text:
## Key supporting enums (classification, not status)

- `eUserType` — Falcon(1) / Client(2)
- `eUserRoles` — SystemAdministrator(1) / Product(2) / Operation(3) / AccountOwner(4) / NodeAdmin(5) / NormalUser(6)
- `ePasswordSecurityLevel` — Normal(1) / Advanced(2)
- `eClassificationCategory` — VIP(1) / Critical(2) / Normal(3)
- `eClassificationSubCategory` — Bank/Gov/SemiGov/LargeEnterprise/MediumEntity/SME
- `eSector` — Government(1) / Commercial(2) / Charity(3)
- `eAuthorityLetterType` — Government(1) / Commercial(2) / Charity(3)
- `eCurrency` — SAR(1) / Points(2)
- `eWalletType` — MasterWallet(1) / NodeWallet(2) / UserWallet(3) / CommChannelWallet(4)
- `ePricingType` — None(0) / Monthly(1) / Yearly(2) / OneTimePayment(3)

heading: Drift watch
text:
## Drift watch

- `eUserStatus` is **duplicated** between Identity and Commerce — keep in sync.
- `eFalconServiceStatus` (Commerce) and `eProductSubscriptionStatus` (Provisioning) overlap conceptually but use **different integer values**. Cross-service serialization must use named enums.
- `eUserRoles` and `eUserType` are duplicated **three** times: Identity, Commerce, Provisioning.

| Drift | What | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|

| PasswordSecurityLevel vocabulary | PRD `Normal/Advanced`, backend `Low/Medium/High/Strict` | Display PRD labels, submit backend codes |

heading: Falcon UI Core (Library Hub)
text: # Falcon UI Core (Library Hub)

heading: What it is
text:
## What it is
Falcon UI Core is the **only** design-system library on the Falcon platform. Every reusable UI component — atoms, molecules, organisms — lives here. Built dual-render: Stencil Shadow DOM + Tailwind v4 Light DOM (per `feedback_shadow_is_token_ssot` rule). No PrimeNG, no other UI kit.

heading: Where it lives
text:
## Where it lives
- **Package:** `@falcon/ui-core`
- **Repo path:** `_mounts/services/falcon-web-platform-ui/libs/falcon-ui-core/`
- **Tokens companion:** `libs/falcon-ui-tokens` (re-exported under the same package)
- **Theme SoT:** `_mounts/theme/`

heading: Why one library
text:
## Why one library
- **One import surface** — pages import a single package, not 60 separate packages
- **Atomic versioning** — bumping `@falcon/ui-core` upgrades every component together
- **Single SoT for tokens** — design tokens declared once, every component consumes the same vars
- **Auto-promotion rule** — when a page using these components is approved by Ammar, every component used on it auto-promotes its capability score per `Brain SK/skills/component-capability-upgrade`

heading: Rules (from project memory)
text:
## Rules (from project memory)
- **Tailwind utilities on templates only** — no SCSS, no component CSS (`project_brain_skills_primeng_purge`)
- **Shadow + `<name>.tokens.css` is SoT** — Tailwind variant mirrors the same tokens (`feedback_shadow_is_token_ssot`)
- **Zero PrimeNG, zero PrimeIcons** — all icons via vendored Falcon icon font (`project_falcon_primeng_total_removal_complete`)
- **Forward-only color naming** — `falcon-{family}-{shade}` per Noor Instructions (`feedback_noor_instructions`)

> [!tldr]
> PES (Policy Evaluation Service) is Falcon's PBAC (policy-based access control) engine. Stores two rule types in Mongo: `p` (role → resource/action permissions) and `g` (user → role bindings), and evaluates `authorize(subject, resource, action)` requests. The frontend is the primary caller; gateways do not call PES.

heading: falcon-core-access-svc (PES)
text: # falcon-core-access-svc (PES)

heading: What it owns
text:
## What it owns

- The **policy database** — every role's `p` rules (what the role can do) + every user's `g` rules (what role the user has).
- The **decision point** — `DecisionPoint.LoadPolicyRules` matches `(p.sub = role)` against `(g.sub = role AND g.obj = user)` to resolve effective permissions for a subject.
- The **built-in role catalog** — `BuiltInRoleCatalog.cs` defines the 6 canonical Falcon roles (3 system + 3 account) and their default `p`-rule set. Provisioned per tenant on first access via `BuiltInRoleProvisioner`.

heading: Rule types
text:
## Rule types

| Type | Subject (`sub`) | Object (`obj`) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `p` | `r:<role-key>@<ns>` | `<resource>` | This role can do `action` on `resource` |
| `g` | `r:<role-key>@<ns>` | `u:<user-id>@<ns>` | This user has this role |

`ns` (namespace) = `system` for Falcon users, `<tenantId>` for Client users. See [[PES-Subject-Contract]] for the canonical subject format + the bug it documents.

heading: Built-in roles (source: `BuiltInRoleCatalog.cs`)
text:
## Built-in roles (source: `BuiltInRoleCatalog.cs`)

| Role key | Display | Type | Pages | Default `p`-rule count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sys-admin` | System Administrator | Falcon | admin-console (all) | 67 |
| `sys-ops` | System Operation | Falcon | admin-console (hierarchy + ops) | 55 |
| `sys-products` | Products | Falcon | admin-console (commerce + wallet) | 65 |
| `acc-owner` | Account Owner | Client | management-console (all) | 31 |
| `acc-admin` | Node Admin | Client | management-console (org + users) | 29 |
| `acc-user` | Normal User | Client | management-console (contact-group only) | 32 |

Self/Other role-edit rules (`user.role.self/set-<role>`, `user.role.other/change-<a>-to-<b>`) are auto-generated by `BuildSelfRoleEditPolicies` / `BuildOtherRoleEditPolicies` and not listed in the per-role count above.

> [!tldr]
> Falcon's identity authority — owns the user lifecycle (create / update / suspend / delete), the multi-step login flow (password → OTP → token), Zitadel as the underlying OIDC provider, and the policy-subject sync to PES. **Frontend never talks to Zitadel directly** — every auth call goes through this service.

heading: falcon-core-identity-svc
text: # falcon-core-identity-svc

heading: What it owns
text:
## What it owns

- **User lifecycle** — create / update / status changes. Identity is the only writer of `FalconIdentityDb.Users` and the only caller of Zitadel mgmt APIs for user provisioning.
- **Login orchestration** — multi-step: `LoginProcess` → optional `VerifyOtpProcess` → optional `SetPasswordProcess`. Each step returns a `LoginStepResponse` with a `stage` enum so the FE knows what to render next.
- **Token issuance** — Zitadel does the actual OIDC dance under the hood; Identity wraps the call (`ZitadelAuthService.CreateAuthRequestAsync` + `ExchangeSessionForTokenAsync`).
- **PES policy-subject sync** — when a user is created or has their role changed, Identity calls `AccessRoleLinkClient.SyncPrimaryRoleAsync(user.IdentityUserId, ...)`. The `IdentityUserId` field stores the **Zitadel user id** — this is the value that lands in `JWT.sub` and what every `g`-rule's `obj` must match. See [[PES-Subject-Contract]].
- **Tenant settings sync** — IP allowlist, password security level — consumed via Kafka from Commerce, applied to Zitadel + cached locally.

heading: Login stages (from `eAuthenticationStage`)
text:
## Login stages (from `eAuthenticationStage`)

| Stage | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `PasswordRequired` | Initial — user submitted username only |
| 2 | `OtpRequired` | Password accepted, OTP challenge issued (returns `sessionId`, `devOtpCode` in dev) |
| 3 | `PasswordChangeRequired` | First-login or admin-forced password change |
| 4 | `Authenticated` | Done — returns `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `idToken` |

`Security:OtpRequiredOnLogin = false` short-circuits stage 2 for non-Pending users. See [[Local-Auth-Recipe]].

- Zitadel adapter: `src/Falcon.Identity.Api/Infrastructure/Identity/Services/`

heading: Configuration (env vars — source: `appsettings.json` + `docker-compose.yml`)
text:
## Configuration (env vars — source: `appsettings.json` + `docker-compose.yml`)

| Key | Required | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `Zitadel__Domain` / `__AuthorityDomain` / `__BackchannelDomain` | yes | OIDC issuer URLs (front-channel vs back-channel) |
| `Zitadel__Initialization__AdminAccessToken` | yes | IAM_OWNER PAT for mgmt API calls |
| `Zitadel__Initialization__LoginClientAccessToken` | yes | Login client PAT for session API |
| `Zitadel__Initialization__FalconProjectId` | yes | OIDC project — token audience |
| `Zitadel__Initialization__WebPlatformUiClientId` | yes | host-app OIDC client id — used in `CreateAuthRequestAsync` |
| `Zitadel__Initialization__WebPlatformRedirectUris__0` | yes | Must match the Zitadel `host-app` redirect URI registered by `seed.sh` (`http://localhost:4200/auth/callback`) |
| `Zitadel__Initialization__WebPlatformPostLogoutRedirectUris__0` | yes | `http://localhost:4200/signedout` |
| `Security__OtpRequiredOnLogin` | optional | Dev: set `"false"` to skip OTP step. Production: leave default `true`. |

**Trap:** Missing any of those four `Initialization__*` values → `CreateAuthRequestAsync` throws `FalconException(UnknownError)` → login returns `HTTP 400 "An unknown error occurred."` for every user. See [[Local-Backend-Bring-Up]] for the docker-compose fix history.

> [!summary]
> [BRAIN-OUT] `GetAccountHierarchyHandler` does not enforce `OwnerIdNotMatchWithTenantId` for Client users. A Client user passing another tenant's `accountId` receives the foreign tenant's account-level metadata (`AccountName`, `AccountIcon`, `TenantId`, `Currency`, `WalletBalanceType`, `WalletType`). The subtree is narrowed via `_currentUser.NodeId`, but the top-level fields are leaked. `GetSettingsHandler` and `GetWalletSettingsHandler` already apply this exact check — `AccountHierarchyController` is the inconsistent outlier.

heading: GAP-BE-01 — `AccountHierarchyController` Missing Client-Tenant Isolation
text: # GAP-BE-01 — `AccountHierarchyController` Missing Client-Tenant Isolation

heading: What's broken
text:
## What's broken

- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-commerce-svc\src\Falcon.Commerce.Application\Services\Handlers\GetAccountHierarchyHandler.cs:104-108` — `ValidateQuery` only checks `AccountId` is non-empty. No tenant-isolation check.
- [CODE] `GetAccountHierarchyHandler.cs:46-48` — `accountNode` is loaded for the requested `accountId` regardless of caller tenant.
- [CODE] `GetAccountHierarchyHandler.cs:89-101` — `GetAccountHierarchyResult` returns `AccountName`, `AccountIcon`, `TenantId`, `Currency`, `WalletBalanceType`, `WalletType` of the requested account.
- [CODE] `GetAccountHierarchyHandler.cs:66` — `startNodeId = string.IsNullOrEmpty(_currentUser.NodeId) ? query.AccountId : _currentUser.NodeId;` — narrows the **subtree** to the caller's node, but does NOT prevent the foreign account metadata from being returned.
- [CODE] Reference handlers that DO enforce: `GetSettingsHandler.cs:65-69` (`ValidateClientOwnership`) and `GetWalletSettingsHandler.cs:63-65` (inline check in `ValidateQuery`). Both raise `FalconKeys.Error.OwnerIdNotMatchWithTenantId`.

heading: Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **Tenant isolation is the load-bearing security invariant of the platform.** Any controller that returns tenant-identifying data without enforcing it is a multi-tenancy boundary breach by definition.
- **Account name + account icon are tenant-identifying PII.** If customer organisation names are confidential (the common case in SaaS), this is a real PII leak — an enumeration attack against `accountId` values returns a directory of clients.
- **Wallet topology disclosure.** `Currency`, `WalletBalanceType`, `WalletType` reveal the financial configuration of foreign tenants. Useful reconnaissance for a competitor or attacker mapping the platform.
- **Consistency with the platform pattern.** Two sibling handlers in the same module already enforce this check with the same error code. Leaving `AccountHierarchyController` outside the pattern means it WILL be missed during the next security review, and the next engineer reading the code has no signal that this controller is special.
- **Defense-in-depth.** The Core Gateway may or may not block cross-tenant queries at the YARP layer; we cannot assume a single perimeter gate. Middleware-style handler checks are the platform convention.
- **The fix is trivial.** Two lines: one helper method + one call site. There is no architectural debate to resolve, no new error key, no schema migration.

heading: Risk if unfilled
text:
## Risk if unfilled

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| Confidentiality | **HIGH** — foreign tenant `AccountName` + `AccountIcon` returned to any authenticated Client user |
| Integrity | Low — endpoint is read-only |
| Availability | Low |
| Compliance | **HIGH** if SLA / contract promises tenant data isolation |
| Exploitability | **HIGH** — single GET with a guessed/leaked `accountId` over a valid JWT; no special tooling |
| Detectability | Low — looks like a legitimate request in logs |

> [!summary]
> [BRAIN-OUT] `UpdateMainNodeInfoHandler.cs:32-33` has a commented-out role check that, as-written, blocked `NodeAdmin` and `NormalUser` from `PUT /api/Information`. As-deployed, any authenticated user can hit the endpoint. Only the Falcon-vs-Client field-level branching remains as a guard — and that only protects two fields (`AccountName`, `FinanceId`). All other fields write through with no role-level gate.

heading: GAP-BE-02 — `InformationController` Has a Commented-Out Role Gate
text: # GAP-BE-02 — `InformationController` Has a Commented-Out Role Gate

heading: What's broken
Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **The check was written, then disabled without a replacement.** Either it was wrong (then delete the comment + document the intent) or it was right (then restore it). Leaving commented-out security checks in production code is itself a signal that something is unresolved.
- **Backend authorization should never depend solely on the frontend.** The UI hides the Edit button via PES for `NodeAdmin` / `NormalUser`, but a misconfigured FE client, a direct API call, or a future page that forgets to gate would silently write fields.
- **Field-level branching is insufficient.** Today only `AccountName` + `FinanceId` are Falcon-gated. Every other field on the main node — address, phone, district, country, etc. — is writable by any authenticated user including `NormalUser`.
- **PRD authoring is blocked.** The V-rule for "who can edit account information" cannot be authored as a useful contract until the team decides whether the answer is "AccountOwner only", "AccountOwner + AccountAdmin", or "PES-gated per role".
- **Audit-log signal lost.** Without a role-level throw, there is no audit event distinguishing "an admin updated info" from "a normal user updated info" — the latter shouldn't happen and would be invisible.
- **Defense-in-depth.** Production authorization should be enforced at the gateway AND the controller AND the handler. Today it's only at the gateway + a partial Falcon-only field check.

heading: Risk if unfilled
text:
## Risk if unfilled

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| Confidentiality | Low — endpoint is a write, not a read |
| Integrity | **HIGH** — `NodeAdmin` or `NormalUser` JWT can mutate main-node info fields |
| Availability | Low |
| Compliance | **HIGH** if SLA promises role-based change control |
| Exploitability | **MEDIUM** — direct API call with a valid JWT for any non-Falcon role |
| Detectability | Low — no audit trail distinguishes legitimate vs unauthorized edits |

heading: Recommended fix
text:
## Recommended fix

Choose **one** of three paths (Answer B is the legacy intent; Answer C is the modern platform pattern):

**Path A — Restore the original check (legacy intent)**
- Uncomment lines 32-33. `NodeAdmin` + `NormalUser` are blocked. `AccountOwner` and Falcon admins are the only roles that can edit.
- Author V-rule `V-AccountInfo-edit-role-gate` documenting the restriction.

**Path B — PES check (preferred modern pattern)**
- Replace with `_currentUser.Pes.adminConsole.accountInfo.edit` (after confirming or authoring the PES key in `BuiltInRoleCatalog.cs` + `pes-account-role-rules.json`).
- Aligns with `adminConsole.services.editPriceType` / `editPriceValue` / `payment` precedent.
- Cleaner audit trail (PES gate fires before handler).

**Path C — Document as intentionally permissive**
- Delete the comment block.
- Document in the OVERVIEW dossier that backend is permissive by design; FE+PES is the sole gate.
- Accept the defense-in-depth gap explicitly.

**Do NOT** leave the commented-out block in place — that's the worst of all worlds.

Any caller receives `200 OK` with an empty array. The Add Client wizard Step 3 (CommChannel picker) and Step 4 (Application picker) call these endpoints, so their dropdowns are silently empty. heading: GAP-BE-03 — `LookupController` Returns Empty Lists (Add Client Pickers Broken)
text: # GAP-BE-03 — `LookupController` Returns Empty Lists (Add Client Pickers Broken)

heading: What's broken
text:
## What's broken

- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-provisioning-svc\...\LookupSeedData.cs` — both static methods return empty `new List<Lookup>()` / `new List<LookupValue>()`.
- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-provisioning-svc\...\LookupController.cs` — wired to `LookupSeedData` via the query handler.
- [BRAIN-OUT] `Brain Outputs\understanding\backend\provisioning\controllers\LookupController\OVERVIEW.md` — confirms zero records returned regardless of input.
- [MEMORY] `project_commchannels_apps_tabs_backend_integration_plan_2026_05_17` — notes the Commerce endpoints `commerce/Node/{nodeId}/comm-channels/visible/details` + `commerce/Node/{nodeId}/applications` are the canonical sources for per-account picker data — making this Provisioning controller either dead code or a different (master-list) concern.

heading: Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **Add Client is the primary onboarding flow.** Step 3 + Step 4 of the wizard cannot complete with empty dropdowns. Operators literally cannot add a client with CommChannel or Application selections via the wizard until this is resolved.
- **Silent failure mode is the worst kind.** The endpoint returns `200 OK` with `[]`. No error, no log, no toast. FE devs debugging "the dropdown is empty" will chase the FE layer for hours before suspecting the backend.
- **Architectural ambiguity is a tax on every future engineer.** Either Provisioning owns the master lookup catalogue (Path A) or Commerce owns it per-account (Path B). The current state ("Provisioning ships an empty endpoint while Commerce has per-account endpoints that work") is the worst of both — it makes every developer ask "which one do I call?" and the answer "neither — Provisioning's is broken" is not discoverable from the code.
- **Dead-code rot.** If Path B is correct, `LookupController` + `LookupSeedData` + the query types + their tests are dead weight in the deployment. They consume build time, scan time, and review attention.
- **Source-of-truth drift risk.** If both endpoints continue to exist, the moment someone seeds `LookupSeedData` (Path A), the FE may start receiving conflicting values from Provisioning vs the per-account Commerce list.

heading: Risk if unfilled
text:
## Risk if unfilled

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| Functional | **HIGH** — Add Client wizard Step 3/4 dropdowns empty; flow cannot complete |
| Data-integrity | **MEDIUM** — if someone seeds half the data later, FE consumers diverge from Commerce-sourced data |
| Engineering hygiene | **MEDIUM** — dead code with no documentation pollutes architecture diagrams + endpoint registries |
| Onboarding UX | **HIGH** — first impression of Add Client wizard is "broken pickers" |

heading: Recommended fix
text:
## Recommended fix

**Decide which path is correct, then act atomically.**

**Path A — Provisioning owns master lookup catalogue (seed the data)**
- Populate `LookupSeedData.GetLookups()` + `GetLookupValues()` with the canonical CommChannel + Application catalogue from PRD-01 dropdown definitions.
- OR wire a real repository (`IRepository<Lookup>`, `IRepository<LookupValue>`) and migrate seed data to Mongo at first boot.
- Add tests proving non-empty response.

**Path B — Commerce owns per-account picker data (recommended; delete dead code)**
- Update Add Client wizard Step 3/4 to call `GET commerce/Node/{accountId}/comm-channels/visible` + `GET commerce/Node/{accountId}/applications` directly (these already work per [MEMORY] `project_commchannels_apps_tabs_backend_integration_plan_2026_05_17`).
- Delete `LookupController` + `LookupSeedData` + query types + test files.
- Update `ENDPOINT_REGISTRY.md` to remove the dead endpoints.
- Note: Path B closes [[GAP-BE-08-Lookup-Regex-Escape]] and [[GAP-BE-11-Lookup-Case-Sensitivity]] as no-ops (controller no longer exists).

**Path C — Seed file should be loaded at startup, locate the missing asset**
- Code review the LookupSeedData boot sequence; look for a missing JSON/CSV asset path.
- If found, wire the load; if not, fall through to Path A or B.

heading: GAP-BE-04 — Admin OTP Path for Editing Another User's Email/Phone Is Undefined (Q-UM-13)
text: # GAP-BE-04 — Admin OTP Path for Editing Another User's Email/Phone Is Undefined (Q-UM-13)

heading: What's broken
text:
## What's broken

- [PRD] `Brain Outputs\prd\modules\02-user-management\BUSINESS_RULES.md:74` (BR-UM-36) — *"Editable personal fields (admin): First Name, Last Name, Profile Picture, Email (with OTP to new email), Phone (with OTP to new phone)."* The PRD says "with OTP" but does NOT specify which actor receives the OTP.
- [CODE] `apps/host-shell/src/app/features/user-profile/services/profile-otp.service.ts:23-60` — only `/api/user/me/verify-{email|phone}` exists (current logged-in user only).
- [BRAIN-OUT] `Brain Outputs\understanding\backend\identity\ENDPOINT_REGISTRY.md:41-46` — no `POST /api/user/{id}/verify-{email|phone}` exists.
- No FE component handles "admin-attestation OTP", "target-user OTP collection", or "admin-bypass with audit-log".

heading: Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **Edit User is a Wave 4 epic.** Staffing time, backend story points, and FE wizard architecture all depend on the answer. The decision touches at minimum: new Identity endpoints, FE OTP component variant, PES key for admin-bypass, audit-log event types.
- **Security model is not a frontend implementation detail.** Whether admins can change another user's contact details without verification has compliance implications (audit trail, intent attestation, attacker model). This must be a product/security decision, not a quietly-shipped FE behavior.
- **Three paths have completely different surface area:**
  - **Path 1 (OTP to target user):** new endpoints + target-user must be reachable in real time; admin cannot complete the change unless target user cooperates.
  - **Path 2 (OTP to admin):** new admin-attestation endpoints; admin proves intent; protects against compromised admin sessions.
  - **Path 3 (admin bypass):** no new endpoint; new audit-log event; new PES key gating which roles bypass; FE shows different "Save" affordance.
- **UX divergence is large.** Path 1 produces "Awaiting verification" pending states. Path 2 produces in-flow OTP modals on the admin's side. Path 3 produces immediate save with no OTP UI at all. The wizard cannot be designed before this is locked.
- **Cannot author V-rule or PES key.** `V-EditUser-email-change` cannot have a falsifiable contract without knowing which actor verifies. `adminConsole.user.editContactWithoutOtp` (if Path 3) does not exist in the registry.
- **Blocks all downstream work.** GAP-UM-21 (page-level Edit User gap) and the entire `pages/edit-user/05-SECTION_OTP_VERIFICATION.md` flow definition are blocked on this answer.

heading: Risk if unfilled
text:
## Risk if unfilled

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| Schedule | **HIGH** — Edit User epic cannot complete |
| Security | **HIGH** if Path 3 is chosen tacitly without explicit decision — admins silently bypass OTP |
| Compliance | **HIGH** — no defensible audit trail of intent for admin-driven contact changes |
| Engineering rework | **HIGH** — committing to Path 1 then switching to Path 3 throws away 2 new endpoints + FE flow |
| User trust | **MEDIUM** — surprise "your email was changed" notifications without OTP path are jarring |

heading: Recommended fix
text:
## Recommended fix

Product + security decision required before any code change. Recommended sequence:

1. **Schedule product clarification call.** Owner: PM + security lead.
2. **Choose a path** (Path 3 admin-bypass is industry-standard and simplest; recommend with explicit audit-log requirement).
3. **Update BR-UM-36** with the explicit actor model.
4. **If Path 1 or 2:** add `POST /api/user/{id}/verify-email`, `POST /api/user/{id}/verify-phone` endpoints to Identity. Author DTOs, validators, error codes.
5. **If Path 3:** define which roles bypass (Falcon System Admin? Account Owner? Node Admin?). Add `admin-override` audit-log event. Author `adminConsole.user.editContactWithoutOtp` PES key.
6. **Author V-rule** `V-EditUser-email-change` and `V-EditUser-phone-change` with the chosen contract.
7. **Wire FE** profile-otp.service to call the per-id endpoints (Paths 1/2) or skip the OTP flow with audit (Path 3).

heading: GAP-BE-05 — `SettingController` + `InformationController` Missing Class-Level `[Authorize]`
text: # GAP-BE-05 — `SettingController` + `InformationController` Missing Class-Level `[Authorize]`

heading: What's broken
text:
## What's broken

- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-commerce-svc\src\Falcon.Commerce.Api\Controllers\SettingController.cs:18` — only `[ApiController]`; no `[Authorize]`.
- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-commerce-svc\src\Falcon.Commerce.Api\Controllers\InformationController.cs:13` — same.
- [CODE] Reference (consistent) — `AccountHierarchyController.cs:15`, `ContractsController.cs:15` etc. all class-level `[Authorize]`.
- [CODE] Only one action in `SettingController` carries explicit auth (`POST /wallets` → `[Authorize(Policy = FalconOnly)]`). The other three actions (`GET /`, `PUT /`, `GET /wallets/{id}`) inherit no auth at all.

heading: Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **Defense-in-depth is the platform pattern.** Every other controller in Commerce is class-level authorized. The convention exists precisely so that a network misconfiguration, an internal mesh call, or a gateway bypass does not produce a data leak. Outliers are regression-risk because the next security review will scan for `[Authorize]` presence and miss the gateway-only path.
- **`GET /api/Setting` returns `SecuritySettings`** including `AllowedIps` and `PasswordSecurityLevel`. These are sensitive configuration values — an attacker discovering tenant `AllowedIps` learns the firewall posture. An unauthenticated leak of this data would be a real compliance incident.
- **Gateway is not infallible.** YARP routes are configuration. A misconfigured route, a port-forward, an east-west fabric route, or a service mesh fault can all bypass the gateway. The controller `[Authorize]` is the cheapest backstop available — it costs two lines.
- **`PUT /api/Information` is a write.** Without `[Authorize]`, an unauthenticated caller who reaches the controller could mutate main-node info fields. Combined with [[GAP-BE-02-Information-Role-Check-Commented]] (no role check inside the handler), this is a write-without-auth path if the gateway ever fails open.
- **Architecture diagrams imply `[Authorize]`.** Onboarding docs say "every controller is authenticated". The two outliers create a hidden exception that contradicts the documented architecture. Future engineers will assume the docs are true and act accordingly.
- **The fix is mechanical.** Two `[Authorize]` decorators. No new policy, no new error code, no behavior change for any legitimate caller (who always sends a JWT anyway).

heading: Risk if unfilled
text:
## Risk if unfilled

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| Confidentiality | **MEDIUM** — `GET /api/Setting` could leak `AllowedIps` + `PasswordSecurityLevel` to unauthenticated callers IF the gateway is bypassed |
| Integrity | **MEDIUM** — `PUT /api/Information` could mutate main-node fields without auth IF the gateway is bypassed |
| Availability | Low |
| Exploitability | **LOW in current production** (gateway is healthy) but **becomes HIGH** the moment a mesh fault or misconfiguration occurs |
| Defensive posture | **HIGH** — single perimeter security is below platform standard |

heading: Recommended fix
text:
## Recommended fix

Two-line edit. Mirror the rest of the Commerce controllers:

```csharp
[Route("api/[controller]")]
[ApiController]
[Authorize]   // <-- add this line
public class SettingController : ControllerBase { ... }

[Route("api/[controller]")]
[ApiController]
[Authorize]   // <-- add this line
public class InformationController : ControllerBase { ... }
```

**If any east-west endpoint genuinely needs anonymous access** (e.g. Charging reads wallet config internally), mirror the `SecurityController` pattern — class `[Authorize]` plus action-level `[AllowAnonymous]` on the specific east-west endpoint. Do not default the whole controller to permissive.

Any caller with network access to the Charging port can publish to Kafka without authentication. Three additional hygiene issues: namespace is `Falcon.Commerce.*` (copy-paste rot from Commerce), error responses use raw `text/plain` instead of `ServiceOperationResult`, and `TestEvent` uses `DateTimeOffset.Now` (local-time drift in a distributed system).

heading: GAP-BE-06 — `TestKafkaController` Anonymous Kafka Publish in Charging
text: # GAP-BE-06 — `TestKafkaController` Anonymous Kafka Publish in Charging

heading: What's broken
text:
## What's broken

- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-charging-svc\...\TestKafkaController.cs` — `[AllowAnonymous]` on both `POST /api/TestKafka/publish` and `GET /api/TestKafka/health`.
- [CODE] `TestEvent.cs` — namespace is `Falcon.Commerce.*` (copy-pasted from Commerce, never renamed to `Falcon.Charging.*`).
- [CODE] `TestKafkaController.cs` — error paths return raw `text/plain` body; platform convention is `ServiceOperationResult<T>` everywhere (per `C:\Falcon\CLAUDE.md` Platform Standards).
- [CODE] `TestEvent.cs` — uses `DateTimeOffset.Now` instead of `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`. Local-time semantics in a distributed event stream produce ordering bugs across timezones.

heading: Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **Test endpoints should not ship in production builds.** This is a near-universal platform rule. Anyone reviewing the deployment manifest and seeing a `/api/TestKafka/publish` endpoint will immediately ask "why is this here?" — and the right answer is "it shouldn't be."
- **Unauthenticated Kafka publish is a flood-attack vector.** While the Charging port is internal-only in production, the moment a misconfiguration exposes it (mesh route fault, port-forward for debugging, accidental ingress rule), an attacker can flood Kafka with synthetic `TestEvent`s. Consumers downstream then process garbage; legitimate events queue up; latency rises; cost rises.
- **No authentication = no audit trail.** Even legitimate internal callers leave no JWT-derived identity in logs. If the endpoint is ever abused, there's no trace of who.
- **Namespace drift is contagious.** Files in `Falcon.Commerce.*` namespace inside the `falcon-core-charging-svc` repository break grep, break refactor tooling, break service boundaries in diagrams, and signal "this code was never properly owned by Charging."
- **Response-shape drift breaks FE contract.** Platform standards mandate `ServiceOperationResult<T>` everywhere. A controller returning `text/plain` on error breaks the FE error-dialog contract (FE expects `result.code` + `result.message` shape, gets a string instead).
- **`DateTimeOffset.Now` is a distributed-systems bug waiting to happen.** Two services in different timezones produce events that sort incorrectly. Replay tooling that assumes UTC silently misorders. This is the kind of bug that's invisible until production cuts an incident.

heading: Risk if unfilled
text:
## Risk if unfilled

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| Confidentiality | **LOW** — `TestEvent` payload is synthetic, not PII |
| Integrity | **MEDIUM** — anonymous caller can pollute Kafka with synthetic events that downstream consumers process |
| Availability | **MEDIUM** — Kafka flooding could degrade the charging pipeline |
| Compliance | **MEDIUM** — unauthenticated production endpoints are typically a finding in security audits |
| Engineering hygiene | **HIGH** — namespace + response-shape + time-handling drift accumulates technical debt |
| Exploitability | **LOW in current production** (internal port), **MEDIUM** in misconfigured network |

heading: Recommended fix
text:
## Recommended fix

Pick one, in this preference order:

**Path A — Remove from production builds (recommended; cleanest)**
- Wrap controller + 3 test files in `#if DEBUG` conditional compilation, OR
- Move controller to a separate test project not included in the production build, OR
- Gate registration behind an environment-based feature flag (`if (env.IsDevelopment()) services.AddController<TestKafkaController>()`).
- Confirm `dotnet publish -c Release` produces a deployment without the controller.

**Path B — Authorize the existing endpoints (keeps for integration tests)**
- Replace `[AllowAnonymous]` with `[Authorize(Policy = "FalconServiceAuth")]` or similar internal-only policy.
- Rename namespace to `Falcon.Charging.*` in `TestEvent.cs` and the controller.
- Switch error responses to `ServiceOperationResult<T>.Failure(...)`.
- Switch `DateTimeOffset.Now` → `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`.

**Path C — Accept the risk (lowest effort, weakest)**
- Document in OVERVIEW that the port is not externally exposed.
- Still fix the namespace / response-shape / time-handling issues as separate hygiene work.

**Recommended:** Path A. Test endpoints in production builds are an anti-pattern regardless of authentication.

heading: GAP-BE-07 — `SettingController.Get` Calls AutoMapper Twice
text: # GAP-BE-07 — `SettingController.Get` Calls AutoMapper Twice

heading: What's broken
text:
## What's broken

- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-commerce-svc\src\Falcon.Commerce.Api\Controllers\SettingController.cs:45`:

  ```csharp
  return Ok(ServiceOperationResult<GetSettingsResponse>.Success(
      _mapper.Map<GetSettingsResponse>(_mapper.Map<GetSettingsResponse>(result))));
  ```

- The inner `_mapper.Map<GetSettingsResponse>(result)` converts the handler result (`GetSettingsResult`) into the response DTO.
- The outer `_mapper.Map<GetSettingsResponse>(...)` then takes that response and maps it to itself.
- [MEMORY] `project_settings_tab_standalone_wave14_2026_05_17` — Wave 14 Settings tab is in production using this endpoint, so the path does NOT throw at runtime. That rules out the "no map registered" failure mode; either the identity map exists or AutoMapper auto-creates it.

heading: Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **It reads as a bug on every code review.** Anyone seeing `Map<T>(Map<T>(...))` will assume typo first and look up the commit history to understand intent. That's wasted attention on every future PR diff that touches this file.
- **Silent semantic drift risk.** AutoMapper's auto-create-map behavior depends on the version and configuration. An upgrade or config change that disables auto-create would cause this code to start throwing `AutoMapperMappingException` at runtime — a regression nobody is watching for.
- **Performance is wasted (small but free to fix).** Every `GET /api/Setting` request performs an unnecessary mapping. The cost is tiny but the fix is trivial.
- **Future-proofing.** If someone later adds a `CreateMap<GetSettingsResponse, GetSettingsResponse>()` profile (intentionally, for cloning), the double call here will silently follow the new behavior — which may differ from the intent at the original call site.
- **Defense against shallow-copy aliasing.** If the outer call is actually deep-cloning, the caller may rely on receiving a fresh reference. Removing the outer call could break that contract. The fix should explicitly verify intent.

heading: Risk if unfilled
text:
## Risk if unfilled

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| Functional | Low (behavior is currently benign) |
| Performance | **LOW** — marginal AutoMapper invocation per request |
| Code clarity | **HIGH** — reads as a bug; future engineers will misread or "fix" without understanding intent |
| Upgrade safety | **MEDIUM** — AutoMapper version bump that disables auto-map could turn this into a runtime exception |

heading: Recommended fix
text:
## Recommended fix

Investigate then act:

1. **Inspect AutoMapper profiles.** Grep `CreateMap<GetSettingsResponse` in `Falcon.Commerce.*` projects. If a `Response → Response` map exists, document why (cloning intent).
2. **Check git blame** on `SettingController.cs:45` to see if the outer call was added intentionally or as a typo in a refactor.
3. **If typo (most likely):**

   ```csharp
   return Ok(ServiceOperationResult<GetSettingsResponse>.Success(
       _mapper.Map<GetSettingsResponse>(result)));
   ```

   Remove the outer wrap. Single map call.
4. **If intentional deep-clone:**

   Replace with explicit cloning (constructor copy, `System.Text.Json` round-trip, or a documented `Clone()` method). Add a comment explaining why. This is more honest than relying on AutoMapper's identity-map side-effect.
5. **Add a unit test** asserting the response DTO is populated correctly post-fix.

> [!summary]
> [BRAIN-OUT] `LookupController GET /api/lookup-values?name=<string>` passes the user-supplied `name` to a LINQ `Contains` expression that compiles to a MongoDB `$regex` match. If the MongoDB.Driver LINQ translator does NOT auto-escape regex metacharacters (`.`, `*`, `+`, `?`, `[`, `]`, `^`, `$`, `|`, `(`, `)`), a caller passing `name=.*` becomes an unbounded wildcard returning every record. Need to confirm driver behavior, then add `Regex.Escape` if not safe.

heading: GAP-BE-08 — Provisioning Lookup Name Search May Not Escape Regex Metacharacters
text: # GAP-BE-08 — Provisioning Lookup Name Search May Not Escape Regex Metacharacters

heading: What's broken
text:
## What's broken

- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-provisioning-svc\...\LookupController.cs` — `name` parameter passed straight to handler.
- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-provisioning-svc\...\ListLookupQuery.cs` — LINQ `Contains(name)` against the `Name` field.
- [INFERRED] .NET MongoDB.Driver LINQ translator may or may not escape metacharacters before constructing the `$regex` BSON. The team has not confirmed driver behavior; assumption is unsafe by default.
- [VAULT] [[GAP-BE-03-Provisioning-Lookup-Empty-Seed]] — note that if Path B (delete controller) is chosen there, this gap becomes a no-op.

heading: Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **Input sanitization at the data layer is non-negotiable.** Any user-controlled string entering a query must be treated as hostile until proven otherwise. Asking "does the driver escape for me?" is the right reflex; *answering it from documentation* (or by adding `Regex.Escape` defensively) is the right action.
- **The pattern is contagious.** If `LookupController` does not escape, the next engineer copying the LINQ-Contains pattern to a different controller will inherit the same unsafe assumption. The fix here sets the precedent for every future MongoDB search endpoint in Falcon.
- **Disclosure today is low-severity (lookup catalog is read-only and not PII), but the same bug class in a different controller is HIGH-severity.** Treating this as low-priority just because the affected data happens to be benign is the wrong lesson — the right lesson is "we don't escape regex input, and we should."
- **UX surprise.** Even without a malicious caller, a user typing a literal period as part of a search term (`v2.0`) accidentally constructs a regex. The result set is unexpected. Defensive `Regex.Escape` produces predictable behavior.
- **Audit/test debt.** Until escaping is verified or added, the controller cannot be marked PASS in the security-audit checklist for OWASP A03:2021 (Injection).

heading: Risk if unfilled
text:
## Risk if unfilled

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| Confidentiality | **LOW** — lookup catalog is currently empty ([[GAP-BE-03-Provisioning-Lookup-Empty-Seed]]); even when populated, lookup values are read-only and Falcon-seeded |
| Integrity | None — read-only endpoint |
| UX | **MEDIUM** — literal punctuation in search terms (`v2.0`, `name.first`) silently behaves as regex |
| Engineering precedent | **HIGH** — sets the wrong default for every future MongoDB search controller |
| Audit compliance | **MEDIUM** — failed control for OWASP A03 input-sanitization |

heading: Recommended fix
text:
## Recommended fix

Two-step verification then act:

**Step 1 — confirm driver behavior**

Grep `MongoDB.Driver` package version in `Falcon.Provisioning.Infrastructure.csproj`. Read the version's LINQ translator changelog. Specifically check whether `IQueryable.Where(x => x.Name.Contains(input))` performs `Regex.Escape` on `input` before constructing the `$regex` BSON.

**Step 2A — if driver escapes (Answer A)**

Document in OVERVIEW that the driver auto-escapes; add an integration test passing `name=.*` and assert the response is empty (or matches only literal `.*` strings). Close this gap.

**Step 2B — if driver does NOT escape (Answer B)**

```csharp
// In ListLookupQueryHandler, before constructing the query:
var safeName = string.IsNullOrEmpty(query.Name) ? null : Regex.Escape(query.Name);
// ... use safeName in the LINQ expression
```

Or rewrite to use explicit `BsonRegularExpression` with escaping. Add an integration test covering `.*`, `^a`, `a$`, and literal-period inputs.

heading: GAP-BE-09 — `UpdateUserProfileHandler` Permissive on Simultaneous Email+Phone Change (BR-UM-21)
text: # GAP-BE-09 — `UpdateUserProfileHandler` Permissive on Simultaneous Email+Phone Change (BR-UM-21)

heading: What's broken
Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **PRD compliance is a contract.** Either the PRD rule is wrong (then update the PRD with the rationale "BE-permissive, FE-sequential by convention") or the code is wrong (then add the guard). The current divergence means the platform behaves differently from what the spec promises — and which one to trust depends on whoever happens to read the source first.
- **Audit + test debt.** No test covers the BR-UM-21 contract because there is no contract to test. As long as PRD and code disagree, the test author cannot decide what to assert.
- **OTP flow correctness.** If FE issues two OTP requests in parallel after a combined PUT, race conditions on the verification side become reachable (user verifies email, abandons phone OTP, then re-edits email — what's the canonical "verified contact" state?). Strict-reject simplifies the state machine; permissive requires explicit FE orchestration.
- **Defensive UX consistency.** A user changing both fields and seeing two "verification required" notifications creates a cognitive cliff — which OTP came first? Which channel verified? Sequential edits remove the ambiguity entirely.
- **The decision is small but compounding.** Every user-profile-edit feature downstream (Edit User, My Profile, Account Settings) makes assumptions about whether combined changes are allowed. Locking the contract now prevents three FE teams from each guessing differently.
- **Once decided, the fix is cheap.** Either two lines of code (strict-reject) or two paragraphs of PRD note (permissive-by-design).

heading: GAP-BE-10 — BR-UM-29 "30-Min Idle Logout" Configuration Source Undefined
text: # GAP-BE-10 — BR-UM-29 "30-Min Idle Logout" Configuration Source Undefined

heading: What's broken
text:
## What's broken

- [PRD] `BR-UM-29` — "30-minute idle logout" (literal wording).
- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-identity-svc\src\Falcon.Identity.Api\appsettings.json` — `Zitadel:Tokens:AccessTokenExpiry = 1800` (30 minutes). Coincidence is strong but **not labeled** as "idle timeout".
- [CODE] `Domain/Entities/TenantSettings.cs` — does NOT contain an `IdleTimeoutSeconds` field (grep confirmed).
- [CODE] `Application/Users/UseCases/UpdateUserProfileHandler.cs` — does not interact with timeout.
- No `PUT/PATCH` on `TenantSettings` exposes idle-timeout today.
- FE has no explicit `IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` constant or idle-detection logic; logout is implicit when refresh-token retry fails.

heading: Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **PRD compliance audit cannot pass without a definitive answer.** Auditors asking "where is the 30-minute idle logout enforced?" today get a hand-wavy "well, the access token expires after 30 minutes" — which is technically true but doesn't answer the question. Either the spec means token-TTL (then document explicitly) or it means a proper idle timer (then build it).
- **Token-TTL ≠ idle timeout.** A 30-minute access-token TTL logs you out 30 minutes after **token issue**, regardless of activity. A true idle timeout logs you out 30 minutes after **last activity**, sliding window. Users actively working past 30 minutes still get force-logged-out under the current implementation — a real UX bug if the PRD intent was sliding-window.
- **Per-tenant configurable is a real product question.** Some enterprise customers want shorter timeouts (15 min); some want longer (8 hr). If the PRD intent is "tenant-configurable", a `TenantSettings.IdleTimeoutSeconds` field + a `PUT /commerce/setting` patch + FE plumbing + a Zitadel-application-level enforcement mechanism (per-tenant token policy is non-trivial in Zitadel) are all needed.
- **Security stance is at stake.** A short idle timeout protects against shoulder-surfing + walk-away attacks. A long one frustrates active users. Setting the wrong default — or worse, having no enforced default — is a real risk.
- **Compliance frameworks reference idle timeouts.** SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS all reference session idle timeout policies. Saying "we have a 30-min access-token TTL" satisfies some controls but not others (those that explicitly require activity-based timeout).
- **Cheap to close one way; expensive the other.** Path A (document the access-token TTL as the answer) is a 30-min PRD edit. Path B (bui

heading: Why this gap must be filled
text: ld per-tenant idle) is multi-day. The team should pick deliberately, not stumble into a costly answer by accident.

heading: Risk if unfilled
text:
## Risk if unfilled

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| Compliance | **MEDIUM** — auditors flag the divergence between PRD wording and implemented behavior |
| Security | **LOW-MEDIUM** — depends on which intent was meant; current behavior is reasonable but not "idle" |
| UX | **MEDIUM** — active users force-logged-out at the 30-min token TTL is jarring if PRD meant sliding-window |
| Engineering cost | **HIGH** if Path B is the answer and not built; **LOW** if Path A |
| Customer enterprise asks | **MEDIUM** — per-tenant idle is a common enterprise contract requirement |

heading: Recommended fix
text:
## Recommended fix

Two paths; product + security decision required.

**Path A — Document the access-token TTL as the answer (lowest effort)**
- Update PRD BR-UM-29 to read: *"Session validity is enforced by a 30-minute access-token TTL configured in `Zitadel:Tokens:AccessTokenExpiry`. Idle detection is implicit (refresh-token failure → forced re-login). Per-tenant override is not supported in this iteration."*
- Add a `FRONTEND_CONTRACT.md` note documenting the implicit logout path.
- Close this gap.

**Path B — Build a true per-tenant sliding-window idle timeout**
- Add `TenantSettings.IdleTimeoutSeconds` field with a default of 1800.
- Add `PUT /commerce/setting` patch endpoint to set it.
- FE plumbing: an idle-detection service that reads the value, listens to user activity (mousedown/keypress/scroll), forces logout after the configured idle period.
- BE plumbing: application-level enforcement (token TTL is per Zitadel app, not per-tenant, so this needs an application-level guard that checks last-activity timestamp).
- New audit-log events for idle-timeout logouts.
- Tests covering: idle expiry, activity resets, per-tenant override.

**Recommended:** Path A unless an explicit enterprise customer ask requires Path B. The cost-benefit favors documentation.

heading: GAP-BE-11 — Provisioning Lookup Search Is Case-Sensitive (UX Surprise)
text: # GAP-BE-11 — Provisioning Lookup Search Is Case-Sensitive (UX Surprise)

heading: What's broken
text:
## What's broken

- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-provisioning-svc\...\ListLookupQuery.cs` — no `CollationStrength` or `$options: "i"` set on the regex; defaults to case-sensitive matching.
- [CODE] `Falcon\falcon-core-provisioning-svc\...\LookupController.cs` — no preprocessing of search string (no `ToLowerInvariant()` etc.).
- [PRD] `Brain Outputs\prd\modules\01-account-management\latest-prd.md` — silent on case-sensitivity for search.
- [INFERRED] Standard UX convention for free-text search fields in Falcon (and broadly across SaaS) is case-insensitive.

heading: Why this gap must be filled
text:
## Why this gap must be filled

- **Search-field UX expectation is case-insensitive by default.** Anyone typing `whatsapp` expects to find `WhatsApp`. Failing this expectation produces a frustrating "I know it's in the list but I can't find it" loop. Users blame the search, not their casing — and rightly so.
- **The Add Client wizard is the first impression of the platform.** Onboarding flows that feel rough set the tone for the entire product experience. A picker that misses obvious matches in the very first wizard makes the system feel broken even though the data is there.
- **Falcon supports Arabic + English.** Cross-script search expectations are even less forgiving — users typing partial English while looking at an Arabic UI (or vice versa) cannot keep mental track of casing.
- **Workaround at the FE is wasted code.** If we don't fix BE, FE will eventually add `.toLowerCase()` to the search input — duplicating the concern. The fix belongs at the data layer where collation is a one-line option.
- **Consistency with future search controllers.** Setting case-insensitive as the precedent for `LookupController` means every future Falcon search controller inherits the same default — saving every future engineer from re-litigating the same question.
- **Negligible cost.** Single-line driver option. No schema change. No FE change required (and any defensive FE lowercase becomes redundant, not harmful).

heading: Risk if unfilled
text:
## Risk if unfilled

| Dimension | Impact |
|---|---|
| Functional | **LOW** — search still works for exact-case matches |
| UX | **MEDIUM** — first-impression failure on Add Client wizard pickers |
| Engineering precedent | **MEDIUM** — sets case-sensitive as the default for future search controllers |
| i18n / cross-script | **MEDIUM** — Arabic+English users hit casing edge cases more often |
| Workaround cost | **LOW** — FE lowercase is cheap but duplicates concern |

heading: Recommended fix
text:
## Recommended fix

Three paths; Path A is the doctrine-aligned answer.

**Path A — BE case-insensitive (recommended)**

Set the collation on the MongoDB query:

```csharp
// In ListLookupQueryHandler, configure collation on the query:
.WithCollation(new Collation("en", strength: CollationStrength.Secondary))
```

Or use case-insensitive regex options:

```csharp
.Match(x => x.Name.Contains(query.Name, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
```

Or BSON regex with `$options: "i"`. Pick whichever the driver version supports cleanly.

Update `LookupController/FRONTEND_CONTRACT.md` to document the case-insensitive semantics.

**Path B — Accept case-sensitive (status quo; document)**
- Document the constraint in PRD-01 explicitly: *"Lookup search is case-sensitive. Lookup values are Falcon-seeded with consistent casing — users are expected to enter the canonical casing."*
- Author input-help text in the picker UI.

**Path C — FE workaround (cheapest, weakest)**
- Add `.toLowerCase()` to the search input before submitting.
- Only effective if seed data is also lowercase OR BE accepts mixed-case input.
- Duplicates concern; not recommended.

**Note:** If [[GAP-BE-03-Provisioning-Lookup-Empty-Seed]] is resolved via Path B (delete Provisioning lookup controller, use Commerce endpoints), this gap closes as a no-op — and the same case-sensitivity question moves to the Commerce side.

text:
# GAP-NS01 — `@Input/@Output` Decorator → `input()/output()` Codemod

> [!summary]
> [BRAIN-OUT] **871 sites of decorator-form `@Input()` / `@Output()` across 53 files in `libs/falcon-ui-core/src/angular-wrapper/`** need to migrate to the Angular 20+ signal-based function forms `input()` / `output()` / `model()`. **Mechanical but high-volume** — risk is not in any single edit but in workspace-wide template-binding regressions.

heading: Why this is a gap (not a fix)
text:
## Why this is a gap (not a fix)

- [BRAIN-OUT] **Volume**: 871 sites across 53 wrapper components. Too risky to batch into a parallel fix wave.
- [BRAIN-OUT] **Template churn**: every `@Input() name?: string;` migration to `readonly name = input<string | undefined>(undefined);` changes the template-side access pattern from `{{name}}` → `{{name()}}`. Each component's template binding sites must be co-edited.
- [BRAIN-OUT] **Two-way bindings**: `@Input() value` + `@Output() valueChange` pairs need to migrate to `model<T>()` — a different rewrite path than the standalone input migration.
- [BRAIN-OUT] **Partial migration already in progress**: `falcon-popup`, `falcon-notification`, `falcon-empty-data`, `falcon-custom-table-footer` already use the new function form. The remaining ~80% should be completed in one consistent pass.

heading: Inventory
text:
## Inventory

- [CODE] **871 `@Input()` / `@Output()` decorator occurrences across 53 files** per A1 audit
- [CODE] Top concentration files:
  - `src/angular-wrapper/components/falcon-data-table/falcon-data-table.component.ts:68` — highest count
  - `src/angular-wrapper/components/falcon-dropdown/falcon-dropdown.component.ts:26`
  - `src/angular-wrapper/components/falcon-multi-select/falcon-multi-select.component.ts:27`
  - `src/angular-wrapper/components/falcon-insufficient-balance-dialog/falcon-insufficient-balance-dialog.component.ts:26`
  - 49 other files

heading: Why deferred
text:
## Why deferred

- [BRAIN-OUT] **Too risky for parallel batch**: needs a staged codemod with per-component build verification — workspace-wide test churn is unacceptable in a single-night run.
- [BRAIN-OUT] **The signal vs decorator ChangeDetection semantics differ subtly** — needs zoneless smoke testing on consumer apps after each batch lands.
- [BRAIN-OUT] **Consumer apps `host-shell` + `admin-console` use these wrappers extensively** — risk of regression cascade if not staged.

heading: Proposed fix
text:
## Proposed fix

- [BRAIN-OUT] **ts-morph codemod** with these transformations:
  1. `@Input() <name>?: <T> = <default>;` → `readonly <name> = input<T | undefined>(<default>);`
  2. `@Input() <name>: <T>;` (required) → `readonly <name> = input.required<T>();`
  3. `@Output() <name> = new EventEmitter<T>();` → `readonly <name> = output<T>();`
  4. `@Input() value` + `@Output() valueChange` paired pattern → `readonly value = model<T>();`
- [BRAIN-OUT] **Template-side updates**: pair the TS rewrite with co-located template binding updates (`<name>` → `<name>()` where the template reads the input value).
- [BRAIN-OUT] **Batching**: 20–30 components per batch (one family at a time — buttons + inputs + dropdowns + selects + ...), verifying:
  - `nx build falcon-ui-core` GREEN after each batch
  - `nx build host-shell` + `nx build admin-console` GREEN after each batch (consumer impact)
  - Zoneless smoke test on org-hierarchy-page + auth flows
- [BRAIN-OUT] **Reference partial migrations**: `falcon-popup`, `falcon-notification`, `falcon-empty-data`, `falcon-custom-table-footer` already done — use them as the target pattern.

# GAP-NS03 — Host-Shell Auth Feature Rebuild

> [!summary]
> [BRAIN-OUT] **5 SCSS files (~1,720 lines) + 163 phantom `--login-*` CSS variable references + raw `<input>`/`<button>` markup bypassing the Falcon UI library + inconsistent OnPush + decorator inputs** drive the login / OTP / change-password / forgot-password flows in `apps/host-shell/src/app/features/auth/`. This is the largest single-feature regression identified by the night-shift audit.

heading: Why this is a gap (not a fix)
text:
## Why this is a gap (not a fix)

- [BRAIN-OUT] **Multi-day rebuild** — estimated 3–5 days for a token-faithful, library-first reconstruction
- [BRAIN-OUT] **UX decision needed**: phantom `--login-*` tokens were referenced by an external prototype import and never re-wired to Falcon tokens. Either:
  - (a) **add `--login-*` to the workspace registry** (contradicts Noor "palette over intent" and creates a feature-scoped token island), OR
  - (b) **remap each usage to existing `--falcon-*` semantic/palette tokens** (preferred; preserves design system coherence but requires per-screen UX validation)
- [BRAIN-OUT] **Visual regression risk is high** — half of the auth visuals currently come from browser defaults wherever `var(--login-*)` has no fallback (the variable is undefined → declaration ignored). Fixing this WILL change the rendered output.

heading: GAP-OLDUI-01 — Inconsistent URL Prefixes Across Services
text: # GAP-OLDUI-01 — Inconsistent URL Prefixes Across Services

heading: What we observed
text:
## What we observed

- [CODE] `apps/admin-console/.../wallet-balance.service.ts` mixes prefixes in a single file:
  - `api/commerce/accounts/{id}/hierarchy`
  - `commerce/setting/wallets`
  - `charging/wallet/transfer`
- [CODE] `apps/admin-console/.../org-hierarchy.api.service.ts` uses `commerce/Node` (no `api/` prefix, PascalCase resource)
- [CODE] `apps/admin-console/.../contracts-api.service.ts` uses `commerce/Contracts` (no `api/`, PascalCase)
- [CODE] `apps/management-console/.../contracts-api.service.ts` uses `api/commerce/contracts` (with `api/`, lowercase) — different from admin twin
- [CODE] `apps/admin-console/.../testing-charging-api.service.ts` uses `api/testing/charging/...` (always with `api/`)
- [CODE] `apps/admin-console/.../contact-groups-api.service.ts` uses `contactgroup/contact-groups/...` (lowercase service segment + lowercase resource)
- [CODE] `apps/host-shell/.../auth-api.service.ts` uses `auth/login` etc. (no `api/`, no `identity/` prefix — different gateway base URL handles it)
- [BRAIN-OUT] The gateway then strips and re-prepends as needed — but the inconsistency at the client layer is real and surfaces in DevTools, error tracing, and grep-driven refactors.

heading: Severity rationale
text:
## Severity rationale

- [BRAIN-OUT] **Medium severity** — backend still works because gateways normalize, but the inconsistency:
  - confuses grep and refactor tooling (one URL doesn't find all callers)
  - confuses cross-feature endpoint registries (same service appears under multiple roots)
  - makes the URL prefix unreliable as a service identifier
  - increases onboarding cost (new dev can't predict the right prefix from service name)

heading: Proposed fix
text:
## Proposed fix

- [BRAIN-OUT] **Standardise on one convention in the new theme wiring.** Options:
  1. Always `api/<service>/<resource>` (e.g. `api/commerce/contracts`, `api/identity/user`)
  2. Always `<service>/<Resource>` (e.g. `commerce/Contracts`, `identity/User`)
  3. Always `<service>/<resource>` (lowercase resource segment)
- [BRAIN-OUT] **Recommendation:** option 3 — `<service>/<resource>` lowercase, since most existing call sites already use it for sibling resources. Auth (`auth/*`) and dashboard (`testing/charging/*`) can stay as-is — they aren't under `commerce/` / `identity/` / `charging/` namespaces.
- [BRAIN-OUT] Add a project-wide grep gate (`api/commerce/` or `commerce/Contracts` PascalCase) to fail builds during cutover.
