heading: Falcon Template Management - Business Requirements Document (BRD)
text:
# Falcon Template Management - Business Requirements Document (BRD)

Scope: WhatsApp / Meta Message Templates

Version: 1.1  |  Date: 2026-05-10

Converted from the uploaded Template Module V4 notes. Voice/IVR requirements and permissions/role-specific behavior were removed. Internal template governance has been reintroduced as a configurable **Two-Tier Sequential Approval with Any-to-Approve logic** before Meta submission. Technical architecture has been appended to make this a combined BRD + HLD document.

heading: 1. Executive Summary
text:
# 1. Executive Summary

Falcon Template Management enables customers to create, manage, preview, submit, synchronize, and monitor WhatsApp message templates that are governed by Meta. The module provides a business-friendly interface for configuring Meta-compliant templates across the supported categories of Marketing, Utility, and Authentication, then integrates with Meta for review, approval, rejection, status synchronization, and lifecycle updates.

This BRD deliberately focuses on Meta/WhatsApp only. It includes an optional internal template governance workflow using **Two-Tier Sequential Approval with Any-to-Approve logic** before Meta submission. It excludes Voice templates, IVR flows, voice record libraries, SMS, RCS, user role-permission design, Falcon admin behavior, node hierarchy rules, and any non-Meta channel behavior.

heading: 2. Business Objectives
text:
# 2. Business Objectives

- Allow customers to create WhatsApp templates from Falcon without using Meta Manager directly.
- Ensure templates are captured in a structure that can be internally approved when required, then submitted to Meta for review.
- Provide a clear lifecycle for templates from draft through Meta approval, rejection, restriction, deletion, and synchronization.
- Reduce template creation errors by validating names, languages, categories, components, variables, media, buttons, and sample values before submission.
- Provide a live WhatsApp-style preview so business users can understand how a template will appear to recipients.
- Synchronize templates created or changed in Meta into Falcon when the template type is supported by Falcon.
- Maintain an audit trail of internal approval decisions, Meta-facing events, and status updates for operational support and troubleshooting.

heading: 3. Scope
text: # 3. Scope

heading: 3.1 In Scope
text:
## 3.1 In Scope

- WhatsApp message template creation in Falcon.
- Meta template categories: Marketing, Utility, and Authentication.
- Meta-supported template components: header, body, footer, and buttons.
- Template validation and preview before Meta submission.
- Template submission to Meta and receiving Meta review status updates.
- Template status normalization in Falcon based on Meta status and quality signals.
- Template list, details view, Meta status history, and operational actions such as edit, delete, resubmit, and sync where supported.
- Synchronization of templates created directly in Meta into Falcon when the template format is supported.
- Business rules for supported Flow buttons and existing published Meta Flows where applicable.
- Optional internal template approval workflow using one or two sequential approval tiers, where any eligible reviewer in the active tier may approve or reject.

heading: 3.2 Out of Scope
text:
## 3.2 Out of Scope

- Detailed role-based access, user eligibility, account owner behavior, node hierarchy, Falcon admin behavior, or sharing permissions.
- Permission-policy design for who can act as a reviewer. The workflow assumes an external Access Control / configuration source determines eligible reviewers.
- Voice templates, IVR flows, voice record library, audio upload, static/dynamic IVR nodes, or call flow preview.
- SMS, RCS, email, push notification, and any non-WhatsApp template channel.
- Campaign execution, actual message sending, charging, conversation billing, opt-in management implementation, contact-group ingestion, and delivery reports.

heading: 4. Background and Business Context
text:
# 4. Background and Business Context

WhatsApp business-initiated communication outside the customer service window requires an approved message template. Therefore, Falcon must manage templates as governed assets, not as free-form message bodies.

A WhatsApp template may contain static text, dynamic variables, optional media or location headers, optional footers, and optional interactive buttons. Falcon must help customers build these structures correctly and submit them to Meta for review.

Meta remains the authority for final approval, rejection, pausing, disabling, deletion, quality rating, and policy compliance. Falcon stores its own normalized status for usability while retaining the raw Meta status for traceability.

heading: 5. Stakeholders and Users
text:
# 5. Stakeholders and Users

This BRD describes business capabilities from a customer-facing perspective without defining permissions or role-based access. Any authenticated customer user who is allowed by Falcon access control to manage templates can use the capabilities described here. Access rules are intentionally excluded and must be specified in a separate authorization document.

heading: 6. Definitions
text:
# 6. Definitions

| Term               | Definition                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Template           | A predefined WhatsApp message structure that can be reused to initiate or continue eligible business communication. |
| Meta Template      | A WhatsApp message template asset managed by Meta under a WhatsApp Business Account.                                |
| Falcon Template ID | The internal identifier generated by Falcon for tracking a template record.                                         |
| Meta Template ID   | The identifier or name/language combination used by Meta to identify the template.                                  |
| Template Category  | Meta classification for the business purpose of the template: Marketing, Utility, or Authentication.                |
| Template Component | A part of the message template such as header, body, footer, or buttons.                                            |
| Variable           | A placeholder in a template that is replaced at send time, such as `{{1}}` or `{{customer_name}}`.                  |
| Flow               | A Meta WhatsApp Flow that can be launched from a supported template button.                                         |
| Normalized Status  | A Falcon display status derived from Meta status and Falcon lifecycle rules.                                        |
| Raw Meta Status    | The exact status received from Meta through API reads or webhooks.                                                  |
| Display Status     | The simplified final status shown in the UI, such as Pending, Appro

heading: 6. Definitions
text:
ved, Rejected, Restricted, Deleted, Unsupported, or Sync Failed. |
| Approval Status    | The internal Falcon approval workflow state, such as Pending Level 1, Pending Level 2, Internally Approved, or Rejected Level 1. |
| Sendability Status | A technical status used by Messaging/Campaign services to decide whether the template can be used for sending. |

heading: 7. High-Level Business Process
text:
# 7. High-Level Business Process

1. The user opens Template Management and selects Create WhatsApp Template.
2. The user enters basic information: name, language, reference ID, category, and sub-category where applicable.
3. Falcon displays the message structure step based on the selected category and sub-category.
4. The user configures components: body, optional header, optional footer, buttons, variables, samples, media, and Flow configuration where applicable.
5. Falcon validates the template against Falcon business rules and Meta constraints.
6. Falcon displays a live preview and requires the missing sample values or media placeholders needed by Meta.
7. The user saves as draft or submits the template.
8. Falcon checks whether the template requires internal approval based on Template Management configuration.
9. If no internal approval is required, Falcon marks internal approval as automatically approved and submits the template to Meta.
10. If internal approval is required, Falcon starts the Two-Tier Sequential Approval workflow:
    - Level 1 reviewers receive the template first.
    - Any eligible Level 1 reviewer may approve or reject.
    - If approved and Level 2 is configured, the template moves to Level 2.
    - Any eligible Level 2 reviewer may approve or reject.
    - Rejection at any level returns the template for editing/resubmission.
11. After the final internal approval, Falcon submits the template to Meta and stores the initial raw Meta response and normalized status.
12. Falcon receives status changes through Meta webhooks and/or periodic synchronization.
13. Falcon updates the template list, detail view, internal approval history, Meta status history, and normalized status.
14. The user may edit, resubmit, delete, or view the template according to

heading: 9.2 Step 2 - Message Structure
text:
## 9.2 Step 2 - Message Structure

The message structure must be driven by the selected category. Marketing and Utility support the richest message structures. Authentication templates follow Meta-defined OTP structures and have fewer configurable areas.

heading: 9.2.1 Marketing and Utility Template Structure

### 9.2.1 Marketing and Utility Template Structure

| Component              | Required?                     | Business Rule                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Variable Configuration | Required when variables exist | Support number variables such as `{{1}}` and name variables such as `{{customer_name}}`. Require sample values before submission.                                                                             |
| Header                 | Optional                      | Support text header, media header, and location header when allowed. Text header supports limited text and up to one variable. Media header supports allowed image, video, and document types and size rules. |

| Footer                 | Optional                      | Footer text without variables. Suggested maximum: 60 characters unless Meta API validation differs.                                                                                                           |
| Buttons                | Optional                      | Support quick reply, call-to-action, website, phone, WhatsApp call, Flow, and offer-cod

| Preview and Samples    | Required before submission    | The system must show preview and require sample values for variables and media examples where needed.                                                                                                         |

heading: 9.2.2 Variable Rules
text:
### 9.2.2 Variable Rules

- Numeric variables must use the `{{1}}`, `{{2}}` style.
- Numeric variables must be sequential without gaps.
- Name-based variables should use lowercase letters, numbers, and underscores.
- Variables should not be placed at invalid beginning/end positions when Meta rules disallow that pattern.
- Every variable must have a sample value before Meta submission.
- Falcon should detect malformed, duplicate, unused, or unmapped variables.

heading: 9.2.3 Header Rules
text:
### 9.2.3 Header Rules

| Header Type | Business Rule                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Text        | Optional. Suggested maximum: 60 characters. Supports up to one variable when allowed.                            |
| Image       | Optional. Support Meta-compatible formats and size limits. Source notes mention JPG/JPEG/PNG and 5 MB.           |
| Video       | Optional. Support Meta-compatible formats and size limits. Source notes mention MP4 and 16 MB.                   |
| Document    | Optional. Support Meta-compatible formats and size limits. Source notes mention PDF, DOC, XLS, and around 10 MB. |
| Location    | Optional when supported. Used to include a physical location.                                                    |

If a media or location header is selected, text header should be disabled unless Meta supports the combination.

heading: 9.2.4 Button Rules
text:
### 9.2.4 Button Rules

| Button Type       | Business Rule                                                                                 |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Quick Reply       | Allows one-tap customer responses. Labels must be unique and within Meta label length limits. |
| Visit Website     | Supports static and dynamic URLs where allowed. Dynamic URL variables require sample values.  |
| Call Phone Number | Requires country code and valid phone number.                                                 |
| Call on WhatsApp  | Opens WhatsApp chat with the business number when supported.                                  |
| Complete Flow     | Launches a Meta Flow. Only supported Flow use cases should be exposed in Falcon.              |
| Copy Offer Code   | Marketing-only button where supported. Fixed behavior copies the offer code.                  |

Falcon shall enforce maximum button count and incompatible button combinations based on Meta rules.

heading: 9.3 Authentication Template Structure
text:
## 9.3 Authentication Template Structure

Authentication templates follow a more fixed Meta-defined structure for OTP use cases.

| Area                    | Requirement                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Body                    | Fixed OTP message structure using a variable for the verification code.                                                 |
| OTP Delivery            | Phase 1 supports Copy Code. One-tap autofill and zero-tap autofill are future options unless explicitly added to scope. |
| Security Recommendation | Optional text such as “For your security, do not share this code.”                                                      |
| Expiration Time         | Configurable expiry value where Meta allows. Source notes suggest 30 seconds to 15 minutes.                             |
| Message Validity        | Configurable validity period where Meta allows.                                                                         |
| Preview                 | Must show OTP body, security text if selected, and Copy Code button.                                                    |

heading: 9.4 Step 3 - Save / Submit / Internal Approval
text:
## 9.4 Step 3 - Save / Submit / Internal Approval

After completing required fields:

- The user may save the template as draft.
- The user may submit the template when validation passes.
- Falcon generates a Template ID.
- Falcon records creation date and last update date.
- Falcon checks the Template Management configuration to determine whether internal approval is required.

heading: 9.4.1 No Internal Approval Required
text:
### 9.4.1 No Internal Approval Required

If the template does not require internal approval:

- Falcon marks the internal approval state as `AUTO_APPROVED`.
- Falcon submits the template to Meta.
- Falcon records submission date and Meta response after submission.
- The template status becomes Pending Meta Review until Meta status is received or synchronized.

heading: 9.4.2 Internal Approval Required
text:
### 9.4.2 Internal Approval Required

If the template requires internal approval:

- Falcon creates an approval workflow instance for the template.
- The template enters `Pending Internal Approval` state.
- Level 1 reviewers become the active review group.
- If any eligible Level 1 reviewer approves, Falcon moves the template to Level 2 if configured, or submits it to Meta if Level 2 is not configured.
- If any eligible Level 1 reviewer rejects, Falcon marks the template as `Rejected Internally` and requires a rejection reason.
- If Level 2 is configured, any eligible Level 2 reviewer may approve or reject after Level 1 approval.
- If any eligible Level 2 reviewer approves, Falcon submits the template to Meta.
- If any eligible Level 2 reviewer rejects, Falcon marks the template as `Rejected Internally` and requires a rejection reason.
- Only the first valid decision in the active approval level is accepted. Concurrent decisions after the level has already moved or closed are ignored and recorded as ignored attempts if required for audit.

heading: 10. Template Status Model
text:
# 10. Template Status Model

Falcon must not use only one status field. The system should store multiple lifecycle dimensions to avoid ambiguity between internal governance, Meta lifecycle, UI display, and sendability.

Recommended status fields:

| Field | Purpose | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `displayStatus` | User-facing final status shown in lists and details. This is what the mapping matrices define. | `Draft`, `Pending`, `Approved`, `Rejected`, `Restricted`, `Deleted`, `Unsupported`, `SyncFailed` |
| `approvalStatus` | Internal Falcon approval workflow state before Meta submission. | `NotRequired`, `AutoApproved`, `PendingLevel1`, `PendingLevel2`, `InternallyApproved`, `RejectedLevel1`, `RejectedLevel2`, `Blocked` |
| `metaStatus` | Raw Meta status received from API or webhook. | `IN_REVIEW`, `APPROVED`, `REJECTED`, `PAUSED`, `DISABLED`, `DELETED` |
| `sendabilityStatus` | Technical status consumed by Messaging/Campaign services. | `Sendable`, `NotSendable`, `Restricted`, `Unknown` |

The display status must be derived from approval status, Meta status, deletion state, and sync/import state. Messaging services should use `sendabilityStatus`, not display labels, when deciding whether a message can be sent.

heading: 10.1 Recommended Falcon Normalized Statuses
text:
## 10.1 Recommended Falcon Normalized Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Draft | Created in Falcon but not yet submitted to internal approval or Meta. |
| Pending Internal Approval | Submitted in Falcon and waiting for Level 1 or Level 2 internal approval. Not submitted to Meta yet. |
| Rejected Internally | Rejected by an internal approval reviewer before reaching Meta. Editable and resubmittable according to product rules. |
| Pending Meta Review | Internally approved or auto-approved and submitted to Meta. Not sendable. |
| Approved | Approved by Meta and eligible for sending, subject to current quality and policy state. |
| Rejected by Meta | Rejected by Meta. Not sendable. Editing/resubmission depends on Meta and Falcon rules. |
| Restricted | Not sendable because Meta paused, disabled, or otherwise restricted the template. |
| Deleted | Deleted in Falcon or deleted/synchronized as deleted from Meta. |
| Unsupported | Exists in Meta but contains features Falcon does not currently support. |
| Sync Failed | Falcon could not process a Meta template or status event successfully. |

heading: 10.2 Internal Approval Statuses
text:
## 10.2 Internal Approval Statuses

| Internal Approval Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Not Required | Template does not require internal approval based on configuration. |
| Auto Approved | Internal approval was automatically granted because the template does not require review. |
| Pending Level 1 | Template is waiting for any eligible Level 1 reviewer decision. |
| Level 1 Approved | Any eligible Level 1 reviewer approved; workflow moves to Level 2 if configured. |
| Pending Level 2 | Template is waiting for any eligible Level 2 reviewer decision. |
| Internally Approved | Final configured approval level has approved the template. Template can be submitted to Meta. |
| Rejected Level 1 | Any eligible Level 1 reviewer rejected the template. |
| Rejected Level 2 | Any eligible Level 2 reviewer rejected the template. |
| Blocked | Workflow cannot continue because the active approval level has no eligible reviewers or configuration is invalid. |
| Cancelled | Approval instance was cancelled due to template deletion or replacement. |

heading: 10.3 Meta Status Mapping Principles
text:
## 10.3 Meta Status Mapping Principles

- Meta in-review or appeal-in-review states should map to Pending.
- Meta active/approved states should map to Approved.
- Meta rejected states should map to Rejected.
- Meta paused or disabled states should map to Restricted.
- Meta deleted states should map to Deleted.
- Meta statuses that Falcon cannot confidently map should be stored raw and surfaced as Sync Failed or Unknown for support review.

heading: 10.4 Final Falcon Status Mapping Matrices
text:
## 10.4 Final Falcon Status Mapping Matrices

The final Falcon status in the following tables means `displayStatus`, not the full lifecycle state. The full lifecycle is still stored separately in `approvalStatus`, `metaStatus`, and `sendabilityStatus`.

The final Falcon display status is derived from the internal Falcon approval state and the raw Meta template status. The mapping depends on whether internal sequential approval is disabled, configured with one level, or configured with two levels.

heading: 10.4.1 No Sequential Approval Configured
text:
### 10.4.1 No Sequential Approval Configured

When sequential approval is not required, Falcon treats the internal Falcon approval state as automatically approved. The final status is then driven by Meta lifecycle status.

| Final Status (Falcon) | Falcon Internal Status | Meta Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approved | Approved | Active - High quality |
| Approved | Approved | Active - Low quality |
| Approved | Approved | Active - Quality pending |
| Approved | Approved | Active - Medium quality |
| Pending | Approved | Appealed - In review |
| Restricted | Approved | Paused |
| Pending | Approved | In review |
| Rejected | Approved | Rejected |
| Restricted | Approved | Disabled |
| Deleted | - | Deleted |

Business interpretation:

- `Active - High quality`, `Active - Medium quality`, `Active - Low quality`, and `Active - Quality pending` are sendable and map to `Approved`.
- Low quality remains `Approved` if Meta still allows sending, but Falcon should display a quality warning in the list/details view.
- `In review` and `Appealed - In review` are not sendable yet and map to `Pending`.
- `Paused` and `Disabled` are not sendable and map to `Restricted`.
- `Rejected` maps to `Rejected`.
- `Deleted` maps to `Deleted` regardless of internal approval state.

heading: 10.4.2 Sequential Approval Configured with One Level
text:
### 10.4.2 Sequential Approval Configured with One Level

When one approval level is configured, Falcon must complete Level 1 approval before submitting to Meta. Before Level 1 approval, Meta status is `NA` because the template has not yet reached Meta.

| Final Status (Falcon) | Falcon Level 1 | Meta Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | Pending | NA |
| Approved | Approved | Active - High quality |
| Approved | Approved | Active - Low quality |
| Approved | Approved | Active - Quality pending |
| Approved | Approved | Active - Medium quality |
| Pending | Approved | Appealed - In review |
| Restricted | Approved | Paused |
| Pending | Approved | In review |
| Rejected | Approved | Rejected |
| Restricted | Approved | Disabled |
| Rejected | Rejected | NA |
| Deleted | - | Deleted |

Business interpretation:

- `Falcon Level 1 = Pending` means the template is waiting for internal review and is not submitted to Meta yet; final status is `Pending`.
- `Falcon Level 1 = Rejected` means the template was internally rejected before Meta submission; final status is `Rejected` and Meta status is `NA`.
- Once `Falcon Level 1 = Approved`, the final status is driven by the Meta status.
- `Deleted` maps to `Deleted` regardless of approval state.

heading: 10.4.3 Sequential Approval Configured with Two Levels
text:
### 10.4.3 Sequential Approval Configured with Two Levels

When two approval levels are configured, Falcon must complete Level 1 approval first, then Level 2 approval. The template is submitted to Meta only after Level 2 approval. Before final internal approval, Meta status is `NA`.

| Final Status (Falcon) | Falcon Level 1 | Falcon Level 2 | Meta Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | Pending | NA | NA |
| Rejected | Rejected | NA | NA |
| Pending | Approved | Pending | NA |
| Rejected | Approved | Rejected | NA |
| Approved | Approved | Approved | Active - High quality |
| Approved | Approved | Approved | Active - Low quality |
| Approved | Approved | Approved | Active - Quality pending |
| Approved | Approved | Approved | Active - Medium quality |
| Pending | Approved | Approved | Appealed - In review |
| Restricted | Approved | Approved | Paused |
| Pending | Approved | Approved | In review |
| Rejected | Approved | Approved | Rejected |
| Restricted | Approved | Approved | Disabled |
| Deleted | - | - | Deleted |

Business interpretation:

- `Falcon Level 1 = Pending` means the template is waiting for Level 1 review; final status is `Pending`.
- `Falcon Level 1 = Rejected` means the template was rejected at Level 1 before reaching Level 2 or Meta; final status is `Rejected`.
- `Falcon Level 1 = Approved` and `Falcon Level 2 = Pending` means Level 1 has approved and the template is waiting for Level 2; final status remains `Pending`.
- `Falcon Level 1 = Approved` and `Falcon Level 2 = Rejected` means Level 2 rejected before Meta submission; final status is `Rejected`.
- Once both levels are approved, the final status is driven by Meta status.
- `Deleted` maps to `Deleted` regardless of approval state.

heading: 11.2 Template Details
text:
## 11.2 Template Details

- Template metadata: name, ID, reference ID, language, category, sub-category, status, source, creation date, last update date.
- Internal approval information: current approval level, active approval group, internal approval status, last decision, rejection reason where applicable, and approval history.
- Meta information: raw Meta status, Meta template identifier, rejection reason where available, quality rating, last webhook date, last sync date.
- WhatsApp-style preview: body text with sample values, header, media preview or placeholder, footer, buttons, and Flow link indicator when applicable.

heading: 12. Editing and Deletion Rules
text:
# 12. Editing and Deletion Rules

- Falcon shall not allow direct status editing. Status changes must come from Falcon lifecycle actions, internal approval decisions, Meta API responses, or Meta webhook/sync events.
- Draft templates can be edited freely before internal approval or Meta submission.
- Templates pending internal approval cannot be edited.
- Internally rejected templates can be edited and resubmitted to internal approval because they have not reached Meta yet.
- Any edit after internal rejection starts a new approval cycle from Level 1 and keeps the previous approval cycle in history.
- Templates submitted to Meta must follow Meta edit rules. The system must prevent editing fields that Meta does not allow to be changed, such as name and language after creation where applicable.
- Rejected or paused/restricted templates may be editable if Meta allows the specific field changes and resubmission path.
- Approved templates may be editable only within Meta-supported constraints and limits. Falcon must avoid assuming that approved templates are always editable.
- If a template is deleted in Falcon, Falcon shall either call Meta deletion where supported or mark the record as deleted based on integration design. Deleted templates should not be available for new sending.
- If a template is deleted in Meta, Falcon shall reflect the deleted status through webhook or sync.

Delete behavior by lifecycle state:

| Template State | Delete Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Draft | Delete locally or mark as Deleted according to retention policy. |
| Pending Level 1 | Stop the active approval instance because the template is deleted; then delete locally or mark as Deleted. |
| Pending Level 2 | Stop the active approval instance because the template is deleted; then delete locally

heading: 12. Editing and Deletion Rules
text:
or mark as Deleted. |
| Rejected Internally | Delete locally or mark as Deleted according to retention policy. |
| Pending Meta Review | Attempt provider delete if Meta supports it; otherwise mark Falcon record as Deleted/Deletion Pending and continue sync. |
| Approved | Delete in Meta where supported, invalidate sendability cache, then mark as Deleted. |
| Restricted | Delete in Meta where supported, invalidate sendability cache, then mark as Deleted. |
| Synced from Meta | Delete behavior depends on whether Falcon is allowed to delete provider-owned templates; otherwise mark locally hidden/deleted based on product rule. |

heading: 16. Reporting and Operational Visibility
text:
# 16. Reporting and Operational Visibility

- Template count by status, category, language, source, and WABA.
- Rejected templates with rejection reason and category.
- Restricted templates with pause/disable reason where available.
- Templates pending Meta review beyond a configurable threshold.
- Unsupported synced templates by unsupported feature type.

heading: 17. Non-Functional Requirements
text:
# 17. Non-Functional Requirements

| NFR Area     | Requirement                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Availability | Template Management should remain available independently of temporary Meta API issues; affected actions should show clear retryable errors. |
| Performance  | Template list should load with pagination, filtering, and search. Preview should update interactively without full-page reload.              |
| Reliability  | Meta submission and sync should be idempotent and resilient to retries, duplicate events, and out-of-order webhooks.                         |

| Auditability | All Meta-facing status changes should be traceable by timestamp, source, and reason where available.                                         |

heading: 18. Assumptions and Dependencies
text:
# 18. Assumptions and Dependencies

- Each customer account has a configured WhatsApp Business Account and the required Meta integration setup before template submission.
- Falcon has permission to create, read, edit where allowed, delete where allowed, and receive webhook events for templates.
- Media upload and storage are handled directly by Template Management infrastructure using Falcon’s shared object-storage provider, such as Alibaba OSS, MinIO, or another S3-compatible storage mechanism. There is no separate File Storage & CDN Service in the current Falcon service map.
- Flow creation and published Flow selection depend on Meta Flow capabilities and Falcon’s supported Flow builder scope.
- Meta API limits, template rules, categories, statuses, and edit restrictions may change; Falcon should isolate those rules in configurable validation and integration layers where practical.
- Authorization, user visibility, reviewer eligibility, and operational role design are handled outside this BRD. Template Management consumes eligible reviewer configuration or decisions from Access Control / configuration services.

heading: 19. Acceptance Criteria
text:
# 19. Acceptance Criteria

- A user can create a valid Marketing template with body, variables, sample values, optional header/footer, and buttons, then submit it to Meta.
- A user can create a valid Utility template with a Flow button and select an existing published Flow when available.
- A user can create an Authentication OTP template with Copy Code and preview it before submission.
- Invalid template names, unsupported languages, malformed variables, missing samples, invalid media, and invalid buttons are blocked before Meta submission.
- A template requiring internal approval shows Pending Internal Approval until the active approval level is completed.
- An internally rejected template can be edited and resubmitted, creating a new approval cycle from Level 1.
- A Level 1 approval moves the template to Level 2 when Level 2 is configured; otherwise it submits to Meta.
- A Level 2 approval submits the template to Meta.
- A rejection at any approval level returns the template as Rejected Internally with a visible rejection reason.
- If two reviewers act at the same level concurrently, the first valid decision is accepted and later decisions do not change the workflow.
- A submitted-to-Meta template shows Pending Meta Review until Meta returns an approval, rejection, pause/disable, or deletion event.
- An approved Meta template appears as Approved in Falcon and can be selected by downstream messaging modules as a sendable template.
- A rejected template displays Meta rejection reason when available and exposes only Meta-supported edit/resubmission actions.
- A paused or disabled template appears as Restricted and is not available for new sending.
- A template created directly in Meta is synchronized into Falcon when its format is supported.
- Unsupported Meta templates

heading: 19. Acceptance Criteria
text:
are clearly identified without breaking the template list or sync process.
- A template created directly in Meta is synchronized with `source = META_SYNC` and does not require internal approval by default.
- If Meta indicates the template category changed, Falcon records and displays the current Meta category.
- Template details show preview, metadata, Meta status, and Meta event history.

heading: 20. Open Questions
text:
# 20. Open Questions

- Which WABA selection model should be used when an account has multiple WhatsApp Business Accounts or phone numbers?
- Should Falcon support template appeal actions, or only display appeal-related statuses from Meta?
- Should Falcon allow editing approved templates immediately, or initially restrict editing to rejected/paused templates to reduce operational risk?
- What exact subset of Meta Flow creation will be supported in phase 1 versus only using existing published Flows?
- Should unsupported Meta templates be visible to business users, support users, or only in an admin/support diagnostics view?
- What retention period applies to deleted templates, approval history, and Meta webhook history?
- Should approval workflow configuration be owned by Template Management, Access Control, Commerce/account configuration, or a dedicated governance configuration service?
- Should reviewers be resolved dynamically at decision time from Access Control, or snapshotted into the approval instance when the template is submitted?
- Should Falcon support category recategorization when Meta allows or suggests category updates?
- Can a template creator approve their own submitted template, or must self-approval always be blocked?

heading: 21. Technical Architecture / HLD
text: # 21. Technical Architecture / HLD

heading: 21.1 Architecture Recommendation
text:
## 21.1 Architecture Recommendation

Falcon should implement Meta Template Management as a dedicated service responsible for WhatsApp template authoring, validation, preview, submission to Meta, status synchronization, lifecycle tracking, and provider-specific integration.

The recommended direction is:

> Falcon owns the internal template catalog and user experience. Meta owns final WhatsApp template approval, rejection, restriction, and sendability state.

The service should be independent from Campaign Management, Messaging Execution, and Charging/OCS. Downstream messaging modules should consume approved template data through APIs, events, and cache rather than calling Meta directly.

heading: 21.3 Main Components
text: ## 21.3 Main Components

heading: 21.3.1 Template Management Service
text:
### 21.3.1 Template Management Service

Responsibilities:

- Create and update WhatsApp template drafts.
- Validate templates before submission.
- Generate live preview.
- Start and manage the internal Two-Tier Sequential Approval workflow when configured.
- Accept the first valid approval/rejection decision in the active level using Any-to-Approve logic.
- Submit templates to Meta after final internal approval or automatic approval.
- Store Meta template identifiers and raw Meta responses.
- Track display status, internal approval status, raw Meta status, and sendability status.
- Receive Meta webhook updates.
- Synchronize templates created directly in Meta.
- Publish lifecycle events to Kafka.
- Expose APIs for listing, details, preview, submission, deletion, and synchronization.

Recommended database: MongoDB.

Reason: WhatsApp template payloads are flexible and component-oriented. Components, buttons, variables, samples, media headers, authentication configuration, Flow configuration, approval state, and future Meta extensions fit naturally as JSON documents.

heading: 21.3.2 Internal Approval Workflow Engine
text:
### 21.3.2 Internal Approval Workflow Engine

The Internal Approval Workflow Engine manages Falcon-side governance before a WhatsApp template is submitted to Meta. It is optional and configuration-driven. If approval is not required, the template is internally auto-approved and can proceed to Meta submission directly.

The workflow supports one-level or two-level sequential approval with Any-to-Approve logic:

```text
Level 1 Approval
   |
   | Any eligible Level 1 reviewer approves
   v
Level 2 Approval, if configured
   |
   | Any eligible Level 2 reviewer approves
   v
Submit to Meta
```

A rejection at any active level stops the workflow and returns the template to `Rejected Internally` state. The template can then be edited and resubmitted, which starts a new approval cycle from Level 1.

heading: Approval Engine Responsibilities
text:
#### Approval Engine Responsibilities

| Responsibility | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Resolve approval configuration | Determine whether the template requires approval and whether one or two levels are configured. |
| Create approval instance | Create a workflow instance when the template is submitted for internal approval. |
| Track active level | Maintain whether the template is pending Level 1 or Level 2. |
| Any-to-Approve decision | Accept the first valid decision from any eligible reviewer in the active level. |
| Sequential routing | Move from Level 1 to Level 2 only after Level 1 approval and only if Level 2 is configured. |
| Internal rejection | Mark template as internally rejected and require a reason. |
| Resubmission | Start a new approval cycle from Level 1 after an internally rejected template is edited and resubmitted. |
| Final approval gate | Submit to Meta only after the final configured approval level is approved. |
| Concurrency control | Prevent double decisions by using optimistic concurrency or atomic compare-and-update. |
| Audit trail | Record decision, level, reviewer identifier, timestamp, reason, optional comment, cycle number, and ignored concurrent attempts if required. |

heading: Any-to-Approve Concurrency Rule
text:
#### Any-to-Approve Concurrency Rule

Only one decision can close the active level. The system should use an atomic update condition similar to:

```text
Apply decision only if:
approvalInstanceId = X
AND activeLevel = submittedLevel
AND level.status = PENDING
AND workflow.status in (PENDING_LEVEL_1, PENDING_LEVEL_2)
AND version = expectedVersion
```

If the update succeeds, the decision is accepted. If it fails because another reviewer already acted, the decision is ignored and the API returns the current workflow state.

heading: 21.3.3 Meta Template Adapter
text:
### 21.3.3 Meta Template Adapter

Responsibilities:

- Convert Falcon template model to Meta template payload.
- Call Meta Graph APIs for create, edit, delete, read, and sync.
- Normalize Meta API responses.
- Encapsulate Meta API version differences.
- Handle Meta API errors and retryable failures.
- Keep Meta-specific payloads outside core business logic.

Recommended Application-facing port:

```csharp
public interface IMetaTemplateGateway
{
    Task<CreateProviderTemplateResult> CreateTemplateAsync(
        CreateProviderTemplateCommand command,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);

    Task<EditProviderTemplateResult> EditTemplateAsync(
        EditProviderTemplateCommand command,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);

    Task<DeleteProviderTemplateResult> DeleteTemplateAsync(
        DeleteProviderTemplateCommand command,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);

    Task<IReadOnlyList<ProviderTemplateDto>> ListTemplatesAsync(
        ListProviderTemplatesQuery query,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}
```

Infrastructure may implement this port using a `MetaTemplateGateway`, internally composed of HTTP clients, Meta DTOs, payload mappers, and request executors.

heading: 21.3.3.1 Meta Template Adapter Deep Dive / LLD
text:
### 21.3.3.1 Meta Template Adapter Deep Dive / LLD

The Meta Template Adapter is the anti-corruption layer between Falcon’s internal template model and Meta’s WhatsApp Business Platform APIs. Its purpose is to prevent Meta-specific request formats, API versions, status values, upload handles, error payloads, and webhook payload structures from leaking into the domain and application layers.

Recommended principle:

```text
Application layer speaks Falcon language.
Meta Adapter speaks Meta Graph API language.
```

heading: Adapter Responsibilities
text:
#### Adapter Responsibilities

| Responsibility | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Payload mapping | Convert Falcon template documents into Meta `message_templates` create/edit/delete/read payloads. |
| Component mapping | Convert Falcon header/body/footer/buttons/Flow/authentication components into Meta component structures. |
| Media handling | Upload template sample media to Meta when required and inject the returned media handle into the template payload. |
| Flow handling | Convert Falcon Flow references into Meta-supported Flow button definitions. |
| Response normalization | Convert Meta responses into Falcon result objects with stable status, error, trace, and retry metadata. |
| Error normalization | Convert Meta errors into Falcon error codes such as `META_TEMPLATE_NAME_DUPLICATE` or `META_MEDIA_UPLOAD_FAILED`. |
| Idempotency support | Prevent duplicate submission effects when retrying Falcon commands. |
| API version isolation | Keep Meta Graph API version details inside the adapter. |
| Import/sync mapping | Convert templates fetched from Meta into Falcon template documents or `UNSUPPORTED_BY_FALCON` records. |
| Raw payload preservation | Store sanitized raw Meta payloads for support and debugging. |

Falcon-to-Meta Payload Mapping Example
Falcon-to-Meta Payload Mapping Example
Component Mapping Rules
text:
#### Component Mapping Rules

| Falcon Component | Meta Component | Adapter Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text header | `HEADER` with `format: TEXT` | Copy text and map one variable sample if present. |
| Image/video/document header | `HEADER` with media format | Upload Falcon media asset to Meta and inject returned handle. |
| Location header | `HEADER` / location-supported format | Map only if supported by current Meta rule snapshot and feature flags. |
| Body | `BODY` | Normalize variables, map named variables to numeric placeholders, include examples. |
| Footer | `FOOTER` | Copy text; ensure variables are not included. |
| Quick reply buttons | `BUTTONS` | Map to quick reply button objects and enforce count/label rules. |
| URL buttons | `BUTTONS` | Map static/dynamic URLs and include URL examples. |
| Phone buttons | `BUTTONS` | Normalize country code and phone number. |
| Flow buttons | `BUTTONS` | Map Flow ID/action data according to supported Meta Flow template format. |
| Copy code button | Auth/Marketing button component | Map only when supported by category and current feature flags. |
| Authentication template | Auth-specific Meta template structure | Use dedicated authentication mapper, not generic body/button mapping. |

heading: Media Header Submission Flow Inside Adapter
text:
#### Media Header Submission Flow Inside Adapter

When the template contains a media header, the adapter must upload the Falcon media asset to Meta before template creation.

```text
Template submit command
   |
   v
Load TemplateMediaAsset from MongoDB
   |
   v
Read media stream from Object Storage through the Template Management object-storage adapter
   |
   v
MetaMediaClient uploads media using Meta resumable upload flow
   |
   v
Meta returns media handle/reference
   |
   v
Adapter injects handle into HEADER example
   |
   v
MetaTemplateGateway submits message template payload
```

Recommended media upload result:

```json
{
  "mediaAssetId": "asset_456",
  "provider": "META",
  "uploadStatus": "UPLOADED_TO_META",
  "mediaHandle": "2:c2FtcGxlLW1lZGlhLWhhbmRsZQ==",
  "mediaId": null,
  "apiVersion": "v25.0",
  "uploadedAt": "2026-05-12T10:30:00Z",
  "secretVersion": "v3"
}
```

Recommended behavior:

- If the media asset already has a valid Meta handle for the same WABA, file hash, and API version, the adapter may reuse it.
- If the asset changed, the adapter must upload the new file and store a new handle.
- If upload fails with retryable error, keep template in `DRAFT` or `SUBMISSION_FAILED` depending on command design and allow retry.
- If upload succeeds but template creation fails, keep the Meta handle on the media asset for retry, but do not mark the template as submitted.

heading: Error Normalization Examples
text:
#### Error Normalization Examples

Meta errors should be converted into stable Falcon errors.

Example normalized error:

```json
{
  "falconErrorCode": "META_TEMPLATE_NAME_DUPLICATE",
  "message": "A template with this name and language already exists in Meta.",
  "retryable": false,
  "provider": "META",
  "providerErrorCode": "100",
  "providerErrorSubcode": "2388024",
  "providerTraceId": "A1b2C3",
  "sanitizedRawError": {
    "message": "Duplicate template name",
    "type": "OAuthException",
    "code": 100
  }
}
```

Recommended Falcon error categories:

```text
META_AUTH_FAILED
META_PERMISSION_DENIED
META_WABA_NOT_FOUND
META_TEMPLATE_NAME_DUPLICATE
META_TEMPLATE_VALIDATION_FAILED
META_TEMPLATE_POLICY_REJECTED
META_MEDIA_UPLOAD_FAILED
META_MEDIA_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED
META_FLOW_NOT_FOUND
META_FLOW_NOT_PUBLISHED
META_RATE_LIMITED
META_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE
META_UNKNOWN_ERROR
```

Retry guidance:

| Error Type | Retry? | Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rate limit / temporary Meta outage | Yes | Retry with backoff and outbox/job state. |
| Network timeout | Yes | Retry idempotently. |
| Invalid template payload | No | Return validation-like error to user/support. |
| Duplicate name | No | User must change name/language or sync existing template. |
| Token expired | Maybe | Resolve token again from Vault and retry once. |
| Permission denied | No automatic retry | Raise provisioning/credential issue. |
| Media type unsupported | No | User must replace media. |

heading: Raw Payload Storage Guidance
text:
#### Raw Payload Storage Guidance

The adapter should preserve sanitized raw payloads for support, but it must not store access tokens or sensitive secrets.

Recommended fields in template document:

```json
{
  "meta": {
    "templateId": "123456789",
    "wabaId": "987654321",
    "graphApiVersion": "v25.0",
    "lastCreateRequestHash": "sha256:abc123",
    "lastCreateResponse": {
      "id": "123456789",
      "status": "PENDING"
    },
    "lastError": null,
    "secretVersionUsed": "v3"
  }
}
```

Recommended raw request storage approach:

- Store request hash by default.
- Store sanitized payload only in debug/support mode or raw event collection with retention.
- Never store the access token.
- Never store full media binary in MongoDB.

heading: Import / Sync Mapping from Meta to Falcon
Handling Imported Templates that Contain Media
text:
#### Handling Imported Templates that Contain Media

Imported templates from Meta may contain media header references or sample handles, but Falcon may not have the original media file in its object storage. The adapter must not assume that a Meta media handle can always be downloaded, reused forever, or used as Falcon’s source file.

Recommended import policy:

```text
If template was created in Falcon:
    Falcon has TemplateMediaAsset and original file in object storage.
    Template can show full media preview from Falcon storage.

If template was created directly in Meta:
    Falcon may only have Meta component metadata and media handle/reference.
    Falcon should import the template as supported but media-source-limited, unless original media can be safely retrieved and stored.
```

Recommended media import states:

```text
META_REFERENCE_ONLY
FALCON_MEDIA_AVAILABLE
MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_NOT_SUPPORTED
MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_FAILED
MEDIA_RELINK_REQUIRED
UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_COMPONENT
```

Recommended behavior for imported media templates:

| Situation | Falcon Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Meta template has media header handle but Falcon has no original file | Import template with `META_REFERENCE_ONLY`; show media placeholder or Meta reference indicator. |
| Meta exposes enough media metadata but not the binary | Store metadata only; do not create a fake Falcon media asset. |
| Falcon can safely download/retrieve media binary | Store binary through the Template Management object-storage adapter, create `TemplateMediaAsset`, and set state to `FALCON_MEDIA_AVAILABLE`. |
| Media type is unsupported by Falcon | Import record as `UNSUPPORTED_BY_FALCON` or `SUPPORTED_READ_ONLY` depending on product rule. |
| User tries to edit imported media template | Require user to re-upload media into F

text:
alcon before allowing resubmission. |
| User only wants to send using imported approved template | Allow sendability if Meta status is approved and Messaging service has enough metadata. |

Recommended imported media model:

```json
{
  "importedMedia": {
    "mode": "META_REFERENCE_ONLY",
    "metaHeaderHandle": "2:aW1wb3J0ZWQtaGFuZGxl",
    "metaMediaId": null,
    "falconMediaAssetId": null,
    "contentType": "image/png",
    "fileName": null,
    "downloadStatus": "NOT_AVAILABLE",
    "previewMode": "PLACEHOLDER",
    "requiresRelinkBeforeEdit": true,
    "lastCheckedAt": "2026-05-12T12:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

Recommended UI behavior for imported media:

- Show a clear label: `Media was imported from Meta; original file is not stored in Falcon`.
- Show a placeholder if no Falcon preview file exists.
- Allow viewing metadata such as media type and component type.
- Require `Replace media` before editing/resubmitting a template that needs a media header.
- Do not expose the raw Meta handle to end users unless needed in support diagnostics.

heading: Import Support Classification
text:
#### Import Support Classification

The adapter should classify each imported template.

```text
SUPPORTED_FULL
SUPPORTED_READ_ONLY
SUPPORTED_MEDIA_RELINK_REQUIRED
UNSUPPORTED_BY_FALCON
SYNC_FAILED
```

Classification examples:

| Classification | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `SUPPORTED_FULL` | Falcon can represent and edit the template safely. |
| `SUPPORTED_READ_ONLY` | Falcon can display and use the template but should not allow editing. |
| `SUPPORTED_MEDIA_RELINK_REQUIRED` | Template is supported, but media must be re-uploaded before edit/resubmit. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_BY_FALCON` | Template contains components Falcon does not support. |
| `SYNC_FAILED` | Adapter could not parse or map the Meta payload. |

heading: Adapter Idempotency and Request Hashing
text:
#### Adapter Idempotency and Request Hashing

Template submission may be retried due to timeouts or Meta temporary failures. The adapter should support idempotent behavior through Falcon-side request tracking.

Recommended fields:

```json
{
  "submission": {
    "requestHash": "sha256:abc123",
    "attemptNo": 2,
    "lastAttemptAt": "2026-05-12T12:10:00Z",
    "lastResult": "TIMEOUT_RETRYING",
    "metaTemplateId": null
  }
}
```

Recommended behavior:

- Compute a stable hash of the Meta create-template payload excluding access token and transient fields.
- If the same request is retried, reuse the same submission attempt record.
- If Meta returns duplicate-name after a timeout, run a follow-up `GetTemplates` lookup by name/language to determine whether the previous attempt succeeded.
- Do not create multiple Falcon templates for the same WABA/name/language.

```http

```

The examples below use placeholders such as `{wabaId}`, `{templateId}`, `{flowId}`, and `{phoneNumberId}`. Do not hardcode these values; resolve them through Provisioning and Template Management records.

Create Template with Media Header API Example

text:
#### Sync Templates from Meta API Example

Falcon use case:

```text
Meta template was created directly in Meta Manager and Falcon needs to import it.
```

Meta API:

```http
GET https://graph.facebook.com/{graphApiVersion}/{wabaId}/message_templates?fields=id,name,language,category,status,quality_score,components
Authorization: Bearer {accessToken}
```

Falcon behavior:

- If the template components are supported, create or update the Falcon template record.
- If the template contains unsupported components, classify it as `UNSUPPORTED_BY_FALCON` or `SUPPORTED_READ_ONLY` depending on product rule.
- If the template contains media header references but Falcon does not have the original file, import the template using `META_REFERENCE_ONLY` or `SUPPORTED_MEDIA_RELINK_REQUIRED` as described in the media import section.

Example imported media classification:

```json
{
  "classification": "SUPPORTED_MEDIA_RELINK_REQUIRED",
  "importedMedia": {
    "mode": "META_REFERENCE_ONLY",
    "metaHeaderHandle": "2:aW1wb3J0ZWQtaGFuZGxl",
    "falconMediaAssetId": null,
    "requiresRelinkBeforeEdit": true,
    "previewMode": "PLACEHOLDER"
  }
}
```

heading: Edit Template API Guidance
text:
#### Edit Template API Guidance

Falcon use case:

```text
User edits an existing template where Meta and Falcon rules allow editing.
```

Recommended adapter flow:

```text
1. Load Falcon template.
2. Validate editability using Falcon status, raw Meta status, and Meta rule snapshot.
3. Build Meta edit payload only for fields Meta allows to be edited.
4. Call Meta template edit operation.
5. Store raw response and set status based on Meta response/webhook behavior.
6. If edited content causes template to require review again, move Falcon status to Pending.
```

Important constraints:

- Do not assume every field is editable.
- Name and language should generally be treated as immutable after creation unless Meta explicitly supports a specific operation.
- Media replacement requires uploading the new media to Falcon Object Storage first, then uploading it to Meta during edit/resubmission if Meta requires a media handle.

heading: Delete Template API Guidance
text:
#### Delete Template API Guidance

Falcon use case:

```text
User deletes a template from Falcon.
```

Recommended adapter flow:

```text
1. Load template and Meta identifiers.
2. Call Meta delete operation by supported identifier, such as template name or ID depending on Meta API behavior.
3. Mark Falcon template as Deleted.
4. Remove/invalidate approved-template Redis cache.
5. Publish template.deleted event.
```

If Meta delete fails due to a temporary error, keep deletion as pending and retry. If Meta reports the template no longer exists, treat the operation as idempotently successful and mark Falcon as deleted.

heading: Webhook API Usage
text:
#### Webhook API Usage

Template Management should receive and process Meta template lifecycle webhooks.

Webhook verification endpoint:

```http
GET /api/webhooks/meta/whatsapp
```

Webhook event receiver:

```http
POST /api/webhooks/meta/whatsapp
```

Relevant Meta webhook event types:

| Webhook | Purpose | Falcon Handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `message_template_status_update` | Template approval, rejection, pause, disable, or other status changes | Update raw Meta status, map Falcon status, insert status history, publish lifecycle event |
| `template_category_update` | Meta updates or recommends category changes | Store raw event, update category state if applicable, notify/support based on product rules |

heading: WhatsApp Flows API Usage
text:
#### WhatsApp Flows API Usage

Falcon supports two Flow-related use cases in Template Management:

1. Use existing published Flow.
2. Create a limited prebuilt Falcon Flow and attach it to a template button.

Use existing Flow:

```http
GET https://graph.facebook.com/{graphApiVersion}/{wabaId}/flows
Authorization: Bearer {accessToken}
```

Create prebuilt Flow:

```http
POST https://graph.facebook.com/{graphApiVersion}/{wabaId}/flows
Authorization: Bearer {accessToken}
Content-Type: application/json
```

Example conceptual request:

```json
{
  "name": "Order Feedback Flow",
  "categories": ["SURVEY"],
  "flow_json": {
    "version": "7.1",
    "screens": []
  },
  "publish": true
}
```

The exact `flow_json` must be generated by `FlowJsonBuilder` from a Falcon-supported Flow schema. Angular must not generate raw Meta Flow JSON directly.

heading: Runtime Sending API Boundary
text:
#### Runtime Sending API Boundary

Template Management does **not** send WhatsApp messages.

Runtime sending is owned by WhatsApp Business API Service:

```http
POST https://graph.facebook.com/{graphApiVersion}/{phoneNumberId}/messages
```

Template Management only provides:

- Approved template metadata.
- Variable mapping.
- Sendability state.
- Template components needed by Messaging/Campaign services.

WhatsApp Business API Service owns:

- Runtime message payload creation.
- Sending template messages.
- Sending rich media messages.
- Delivery/read webhook processing.
- Runtime provider errors.

heading: API Ownership Summary
text:
#### API Ownership Summary

| API Area | Falcon Owner |
| --- | --- |
| Template create/edit/delete/list/sync | Template Management Service |
| Template media sample upload to Meta | Template Management Service / Meta Media Client |
| Template lifecycle webhooks | Template Management Service / Webhook Handler |
| Flow list/create/publish for template buttons | Template Management Service / Meta Flow Client, until a future Flow Builder exists |
| Runtime WhatsApp message sending | WhatsApp Business API Service |
| Runtime message media upload/send | WhatsApp Business API Service / object-storage adapter |
| WABA/channel/credentialRef resolution | Provisioning Service |
| Raw token resolution | Vault / Secret Store |

heading: 21.3.3.3 Meta Integration Context and Credential Resolution LLD
text:
### 21.3.3.3 Meta Integration Context and Credential Resolution LLD

The Template Management Service needs `wabaId`, Meta credentials, Graph API version, and provider capabilities to communicate with Meta. However, Template Management should not own WhatsApp channel onboarding, WABA provisioning, or access token storage.

Recommended ownership:

| Data / Capability | Recommended Owner | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WABA ID | Provisioning Service | WABA is part of the provisioned WhatsApp channel/provider asset. |
| WhatsApp phone number ID | Provisioning Service | Phone numbers are channel assets managed by provisioning. |
| Business ID / Meta App ID | Provisioning Service | They belong to provider onboarding and asset ownership. |
| Meta access token | Vault / Secret Store | Tokens are secrets and must not be stored in Template DB, Redis, Kafka, or Angular. |
| Credential reference | Provisioning Service | Provisioning maps account/channel/WABA to the secret reference. |
| Template catalog | Template Management Service | Template Management owns authoring, validation, lifecycle, and Meta template operations. |
| Runtime message sending | WhatsApp Business API Service | WhatsApp service owns sending messages, delivery/read webhooks, runtime media, and provider send errors. |
| Template sample media storage | Template Management Infrastructure + Object Storage | Template Management owns template media metadata and uses an object-storage adapter to create signed upload/read URLs, persist media, and read media streams. |

Recommended principle:

```text
Provisioning Service owns Meta/WABA/channel context.
Vault owns the actual secret value.
Template Management consumes context and resolves secrets only at runtime.
```

heading: Required Meta Integration Context
text:
#### Required Meta Integration Context

Template Management should use a `MetaWhatsAppIntegrationContext`, not only a raw `wabaId` and token.

Example context:

```json
{

  "accountId": "acc_001",
  "channelId": "ch_wa_001",
  "provider": "META",
  "wabaId": "987654321",
  "businessId": "123456789",
  "appId": "1234567890",
  "phoneNumberIds": ["1122334455"],

  "graphApiVersion": "v25.0",
  "webhookConfigId": "meta_webhook_cfg_001",
  "capabilities": {
    "templateManagement": true,
    "templateStatusWebhooks": true,
    "flowManagement": true,
    "mediaUpload": true,
    "messaging": true
  },
  "status": "ACTIVE",

  "timezone": "Asia/Riyadh"
```

Minimum required fields for template operations:

| Field | Required For |
| --- | --- |
| `tenantId` | Tenant isolation and auditing. |
| `accountId` | Account-level ownership and query scoping. |
| `channelId` | Identifying the provisioned WhatsApp channel inside Falcon. |
| `wabaId` | Create, list, edit, delete, and sync templates under the correct Meta WABA. |
| `credentialRef` | Securely resolving Meta access token from Vault. |
| `graphApiVersion` | Stabilizing Meta adapter behavior against API version changes. |
| `businessId` / `appId` | Diagnostics, ownership verification, and webhook correlation. |
| `capabilities.templateManagement` | Ensuring template operations are enabled for this channel. |
| `capabilities.flowManagement` | Enabling Flow list/create operations only when configured. |
| `capabilities.mediaUpload` | Enabling media-header template submission. |
| `status` | Preventing Meta calls for inactive, disconnected, or suspended channels. |

heading: Internal Provisioning API
text:
#### Internal Provisioning API

Template Management should call Provisioning to resolve the active WhatsApp channel context.

Recommended endpoint:

```http
GET /internal/provisioning/meta/whatsapp-context?tenantId={tenantId}&accountId={accountId}&channelId={channelId}
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "tenantId": "tnt_001",
  "accountId": "acc_001",
  "channelId": "ch_wa_001",
  "provider": "META",
  "wabaId": "987654321",
  "businessId": "123456789",
  "appId": "1234567890",
  "phoneNumberIds": ["1122334455"],
  "credentialRef": "vault://falcon/meta/tnt_001/acc_001/waba_987654321",
  "graphApiVersion": "v25.0",
  "capabilities": {
    "templateManagement": true,
    "flowManagement": true,
    "mediaUpload": true,
    "messaging": true
  },

```

If `channelId` is not provided by the caller, Provisioning may return the default active WhatsApp channel for the account, if product rules allow one default channel. If multiple WABAs/channels exist, the user must select the channel explicitly in the template wizard.

heading: Secret Resolution API
text:
#### Secret Resolution API

Template Management should not store or expose the Meta access token. It should resolve the token from Vault only inside the backend execution path.

Recommended internal call:

```http
POST /internal/secrets/resolve
```

Example request:

```json
{
  "credentialRef": "vault://falcon/meta/tnt_001/acc_001/waba_987654321",
  "purpose": "META_TEMPLATE_MANAGEMENT"
}
```

Example response:

```json
{
  "accessToken": "EAAG...",
  "expiresAt": "2026-08-12T10:00:00Z",
  "secretVersion": "v3"
}
```

Template Management may log or store the following non-sensitive fields:

```text
credentialRef
secretVersion
lastSuccessfulMetaCallAt
sanitizedMetaErrorCode
sanitizedMetaTraceId
```

Template Management must not store the access token in:

```text
templates collection
template_status_history
template_raw_meta_events
Redis cache
Kafka events
Angular state
application logs
```

heading: Recommended Application Interfaces
Recommended Application Interfaces
Recommended Meta Client Request Context
Token Caching Guidance
text:
#### Token Caching Guidance

Template Management may cache context metadata from Provisioning for a short TTL, but token caching should be handled carefully.

| Item | Cache? | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WABA/channel context | Yes | Short TTL, such as 5 minutes, with invalidation on provisioning updates. |
| Access token | Prefer no, or very short TTL | Avoid long-lived application memory token cache unless token rotation is well managed. |
| CredentialRef | Yes | Safe to store as reference. |
| SecretVersion | Yes | Useful for audit/debugging. |
| Raw token value | No persistent storage | Never store in MongoDB, Redis, Kafka, logs, or browser. |

heading: Meta Permission Requirements
text:
#### Meta Permission Requirements

The token used by Template Management must have the required Meta permissions and asset access for template management. At minimum, the integration must support:

```text
whatsapp_business_management
```

Depending on the operation scope, Falcon may also require capabilities/permissions related to:

```text
WhatsApp Flow management
media upload for template sample media
business asset access to the target WABA
webhook subscriptions for template status updates
```

Runtime messaging permissions should be owned and validated by the WhatsApp Business API Service, not by Template Management.

heading: Template Service vs WhatsApp Business API Service
text:
#### Template Service vs WhatsApp Business API Service

Template Management should call Meta directly for template management operations:

```text
Template Management Service → Meta Template APIs
```

WhatsApp Business API Service should call Meta directly for runtime messaging operations:

```text
WhatsApp Business API Service → Meta Messaging APIs
```

Both services should resolve channel context from Provisioning and secrets from Vault. They should not share raw access tokens with each other.

This keeps service boundaries clean:

| Service | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| Provisioning Service | Meta/WABA/channel/account mapping and provider asset context. |
| Vault / Secret Store | Meta access tokens, app secrets, webhook verify tokens, and secret versions. |
| Template Management Service | Template authoring, validation, preview, Meta template API calls, lifecycle, and sync. |
| WhatsApp Business API Service | Sending messages, receiving messages, runtime media, delivery/read statuses, and provider send errors. |
| Object Storage adapter inside Template Management | Template sample media persistence, signed upload URLs, signed read URLs, and media streams for Meta template submission. |
| Access Control Service | RBAC/ABAC/PBAC authorization decisions, not provider credential resolution. |

heading: 21.3.5 Template Validation Engine
text:
### 21.3.5 Template Validation Engine

The Template Validation Engine is a backend-owned rule engine inside the Template Management Service. It validates WhatsApp templates before saving, previewing, and submitting to Meta. Angular may perform lightweight UX validation, but the backend engine remains the authoritative Falcon validation layer.

Responsibilities:

- Validate template name, language, category, and sub-category.
- Validate body, header, footer, media, variables, and buttons.
- Validate Marketing and Utility template rules.
- Validate Authentication template rules.
- Validate Flow button and existing Flow selection rules.
- Validate template editability based on current Falcon status and Meta lifecycle rules.
- Return structured field-level errors and warnings.
- Expose validation metadata to Angular so the UI can build dynamic forms and provide instant feedback.

heading: 21.3.5 Template Validation Engine
Rule Context Field Explanations
text:
#### Rule Context Field Explanations

The validation context contains the template draft plus additional data required by rules that cannot validate using the draft alone.

heading: ExistingTemplateNameLanguageKeys
text:
##### ExistingTemplateNameLanguageKeys

`ExistingTemplateNameLanguageKeys` represents existing template identities in the same WABA/account scope. It is used mainly by `NameUniquenessPerLanguageRule` to prevent creating duplicate templates with the same name and language.

Recommended key format:

```text
{wabaId}:{templateName}:{language}
```

Example:

```text
987654321:order_update:en
987654321:payment_reminder:ar
987654321:otp_login:en
```

If the user creates a template with:

```text
name = order_update
language = en
wabaId = 987654321
```

then the engine checks whether this key already exists:

```text
987654321:order_update:en
```

If it exists, the engine returns a field-level validation error:

```json
{
  "code": "TEMPLATE_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS",
  "fieldPath": "name",
  "message": "A template with the same name and language already exists."
}
```

For edit scenarios, the validation engine must exclude the current template itself from the duplicate check. Otherwise, editing an existing template would incorrectly fail uniqueness validation.

heading: WhatsAppTemplateRuleSnapshot
FeatureFlags
text:
##### FeatureFlags

`FeatureFlags` are runtime switches that tell the validation engine which capabilities are currently enabled in Falcon. Meta may support a feature, but Falcon may decide to release it later or enable it only for selected tenants.

Example:

```json
{
  "marketingFlows": true,
  "utilityFlows": true,
  "catalogTemplates": false,
  "oneTapAuth": false,
  "zeroTapAuth": false,
  "copyOfferCode": true,
  "approvedTemplateEditing": false
}
```

Feature flags are used by rules such as:

```text
FlowButtonAllowedRule
AuthenticationOtpRule
CatalogTemplateRule
TemplateEditabilityRule
```

Example: if a user selects One-tap authentication but Falcon has not enabled it yet:

```json
{
  "oneTapAuth": false
}
```

then the validation engine returns:

```json
{
  "code": "FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED",
  "fieldPath": "authentication.deliveryMethod",
  "message": "One-tap authentication templates are not enabled in Falcon yet."
}
```

This is different from Meta not supporting the capability. Meta may support it, but Falcon may intentionally disable it for phase-1 scope, tenant rollout, operational readiness, or compliance review.

Summary:

| Context Item | Meaning | Example Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ExistingTemplateNameLanguageKeys` | Existing template identities in the same WABA/account scope | Prevent duplicate `987654321:order_update:en` |
| `WhatsAppTemplateRuleSnapshot` | Current known Meta/Falcon validation limits and structural rules | Body max length, button limits, allowed components |
| `FeatureFlags` | Runtime capability switches controlled by Falcon | Disable catalog templates, one-tap auth, zero-tap auth, or approved-template editing |

Recommended validation result shape:

```json
{
  "isValid": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "code": "BODY_VARIABLE_SAM
```

heading: 21.3.6 Template Preview Engine
text:
### 21.3.6 Template Preview Engine

Responsibilities:

- Render WhatsApp-style preview using the internal template model.
- Replace variables with sample values.
- Render header, body, footer, media placeholder, and buttons.
- Render Authentication OTP preview.
- Render Flow button preview.
- Highlight missing samples or invalid configurations.

The UI can render live preview locally, but the backend should also expose a preview endpoint to ensure consistent validation and support external API consumers.

heading: 21.3.6.1 Preview and Flow Forms HLD
text:
### 21.3.6.1 Preview and Flow Forms HLD

Preview and Flow forms should be treated as two separate capabilities:

1. **Template Preview**: A WhatsApp-style visual representation of the template currently being authored.
2. **Flow Form Configuration**: A schema-driven way to either select an existing published Meta Flow or configure a small set of Falcon-supported prebuilt Flow types.

Recommended ownership model:

```text
Frontend owns the interactive experience.
Backend owns rules, schemas, persistence, Meta integration, and authoritative validation.
```

heading: Preview HLD
text:
#### Preview HLD

```text
Angular Template Wizard
   |
   | Form value changes
   v
Angular Preview Builder
   |
   | Builds local preview model
   v
WhatsApp Preview Component

Save / Submit / Explicit Preview
   |
   v
Template Management Service
   |
   v
Backend Preview Engine
   |
   v
Normalized Preview Model + Warnings
```

Angular should render the live preview locally while the user types because it must feel instant. The backend should not be called on every keystroke. The backend preview endpoint is still required for consistency, testing, server-side validation, and external API consumers.

heading: Flow Forms HLD
text:
#### Flow Forms HLD

```text
Angular Flow Form Renderer
   |
   | Requests enabled Flow types and schema
   v
Template Management Service
   |
   v
Flow Schema Provider
   |
   v
Flow Config Validator
   |
   v
Flow JSON Builder
   |
   v
Meta Flow Adapter
   |
   v
Meta WhatsApp Flow APIs
```

Falcon should avoid building a full generic visual Flow Builder in Template Management phase 1. Instead, Template Management should support:

- Selecting an existing published Meta Flow.
- Creating a limited set of prebuilt Falcon Flow forms, such as `Get Feedback` and `Send Survey`, using backend-owned schemas.
- Referencing the resulting Flow from a WhatsApp template button.

A full drag/drop Flow Builder should be a separate future bounded context, not embedded inside Template Management.

heading: 21.3.6.2 Preview Frontend and Backend Responsibilities
text:
### 21.3.6.2 Preview Frontend and Backend Responsibilities

| Capability | Angular Responsibility | Backend Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live WhatsApp preview | Main owner; render instantly from form state | Optional normalized preview model for consistency |
| Variable replacement | Replace samples locally for instant preview | Authoritative replacement and validation |
| Header/body/footer/buttons | Render visual components | Validate structure and return normalized preview data |
| Media preview | Show uploaded media or placeholder | Validate media reference, size, type, upload completion, and object-storage availability |
| Authentication preview | Render OTP body, security text, and copy-code button | Validate authentication configuration and return normalized model |
| Flow button preview | Show button and selected Flow label | Validate Flow exists and is published |
| Final preview before submit | Display backend-confirmed preview | Generate normalized preview and warnings |
| Meta payload conversion | No responsibility | Backend only, inside Meta adapter |

heading: 21.3.6.3 Preview LLD
21.3.6.3 Preview LLD
21.3.6.3 Preview LLD
text:
User opens an existing template.
- User imports or syncs a template from Meta.

Angular should not call the backend preview endpoint on every keystroke.

heading: 21.3.6.4 Flow Forms Strategy
text:
### 21.3.6.4 Flow Forms Strategy

Falcon should support Flow configuration in three maturity levels.

heading: Level 1 - Use Existing Published Meta Flows
text:
#### Level 1 - Use Existing Published Meta Flows

This is the recommended minimum phase-1 capability.

User flow:

```text
User adds Flow button
   |
   v
User selects Use Existing Flow
   |
   v
Angular loads published Flows from backend
   |
   v
User selects a Flow
   |
   v
Preview shows Flow button and selected Flow name
   |
   v
Backend validates selected Flow exists and is published
```

Backend responsibilities:

- Fetch published Flows from Meta.
- Cache Flow list by WABA.
- Return published Flows to Angular.
- Validate selected Flow exists and is published.
- Store `flowId`, `flowName`, and button configuration.
- Include Flow reference in the Meta template payload.

Recommended API:

```http
GET /api/templates/whatsapp/flows?status=published&wabaId={wabaId}
```

Example response:

```json
[
  {
    "flowId": "flow_123",
    "name": "Customer Feedback",
    "status": "PUBLISHED",
    "category": "UTILITY",
    "lastUpdatedAt": "2026-05-10T10:00:00Z"
  },
  {
```

### 21.3.6.6 Flow Form Validation Rules

| Rule | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Flow type enabled | The selected Flow type must be enabled by Falcon feature flags. |
| Schema version supported | Submitted config must match the schema version returned by the backend. |
| Required fields | Required schema fields must be filled. |
| Field length | Text fields must respect max length. |
| Option validity | Select/radio values must exist in the backend-provided schema. |

| Existing Flow published | If using existing Flow, the Flow must exist in Meta and be published. |
| Flow name uniqueness | Falcon-created Flow name should be unique within WABA or configured scope. |
| Meta compatibility | Backend must convert Falcon Flow config into Meta-compatible Flow JSON and handle Meta validation errors. |
